9to1 V2 — CUI, THEMING AND REAL-PRODUCT CONFORMANCE CORRECTION
Effective 11 October 2026. User-authorised clarification and refactor contract. The original V2 document remains authoritative; this is not a replacement specification. The canonical CUI and Write sections and the application acceptance rules below have been tightened in place.
CUI-CONF-001–004, CUI-THEME-001–004, APP-AC-001–009, LAUNCH-001–006 and WRITE-AC-001–003 are mandatory. A renamed AXAML surface, native-theme workaround, disconnected test harness, missing donor functionality or attractive but unusable shell cannot satisfy these requirements. Launch/start screens must be distinct product experiences, not headers or introductory sections stacked above the working app; the Launch Screens section defines their identity, transitions and acceptance. Preserve mature engines and working functionality while correcting their public CUI integration.
The active four-part delivery plan below is unchanged: Part 1 full core and donor-complete RCVP foundations; Part 2 the specified Full upgrades and remaining-app RCVP work; Part 3 every-app RCVP reconciliation then Full non-OS ecosystem; Part 4 9to1OS. RCVP may defer only the explicitly staged new enhancements, never donor-complete product-category behaviour, the canonical CUI boundary or essential safety, accessibility and persistence. Historical Pass/priority/deadline material describes retained requirements and provenance, not an alternative current schedule. No agent may weaken requirements or manufacture exceptions to make its implementation pass.

C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
CUI-EDITOR-101 — Shared floating menu contract. First-party File/Edit/Insert/Slide/Arrange/View/Help menus, + Insert menu, shape gallery, font dropdowns, colour popovers, toolbar overflow, right-click context menus and related tool surfaces MUST follow the same CUI-driven design language. Use dark floating surfaces with generous rounded corners, controlled elevation/soft contrast, comfortable but proportional padding, legible typography, icons where helpful, tidy section separators, shortcut labels and correct hover/pressed/focus/selected/disabled states. The dark rounded permissions-menu screenshot supplied during acceptance is the visual style reference, NOT its permission content. Short menus may be compact; this is not a requirement to oversize all popovers. Avoid native Avalonia-styled dropdowns or OS-default chrome in first-party UI.

source_text: CUI-EDITOR-103 — Professional app theme. Use the supplied dark Unsloth Library reference for the overall restrained, modern, spacious professional aesthetic: cohesive dark palette, calm hierarchy, deliberately aligned title/status/header actions, subtle surfaces, softer appropriate rounding, consistent typography and clean panel separation. Do not copy external branding. The selected/hovered states must remain accessible and sufficiently visible. Use the 9to1 CUI theme's declared tokens; do not introduce one-off native-control overrides to imitate screenshots.

source_text: CUI-EDITOR-104 — Icons must be reliable. Icons SHOULD be coherent, moderately rounded, optically centred, consistent in stroke/weight and recognisable, optionally with restrained semantic colour accents. Prefer proven audited icon assets to improvised generated SVG paths. Validate custom icons for viewBox/path integrity, clipping, scaling, stroke, alignment and normal/dark/focus/disabled presentation at ACTUAL toolbar pixel size. A syntactically valid SVG that looks broken is an acceptance failure.

source_text: CUI-EDITOR-105 — Shared abstractions not forced layouts. Reusable CUI EditorShell/EditorToolbar, grouped commands, contextual inspector, menu/popover, insertion catalogue, selection-adorners and viewport contracts SHOULD be extended/shared where justified, with clear source ownership and typed interfaces. This sets shared standards for Write, Present, Data, Boards, Canvas and relevant apps, but MUST NOT force a Present three-row header or object-selection model onto applications whose category workflows require other layouts. D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
STARTUP-UX-101 — No prolonged blank refresh. The observed Present refresh shows a white 'Opening 9to1...' screen for approximately 5–10 seconds. MUST instrument and correct the underlying delay, not merely hide it. Record cold start, warm start, page refresh, within-app navigation, document reopen and loading of larger presentations separately. Measure shell-visible time, document-visible time, time-to-interactive, stage timings and variability. Investigate repeated CUI/Avalonia/service initialisation, blocking UI-thread work, redundant layout or rendering, file/deserialisation, font/assets, state restoration and unnecessary requests based on actual trace evidence.

source_text: STARTUP-UX-102 — Theme-safe progressive startup. The earliest host/shell render MUST use the appropriate CUI theme with no avoidable white flash. Render the real navigation/editor shell promptly where feasible, then contextual truthful loading states for document-dependent regions; do not force full-screen blocking for a small delayed component. Use correctly persisted theme preference/fallback per CUI-THEME rules, meaningful retry/error/recovery states and no fake progress or indefinite splash. Do not expose a native themed interim shell.

source_text: STARTUP-UX-103 — Provisional performance budgets. Target initial visible shell under 1 second, typical warm/reopened document under 2 seconds and ordinary basic editor interactivity under 3 seconds on the specified test hardware/runtime, where practical. These are engineering acceptance goals, not guarantees or previously measured facts. Any missed target requires baseline/after metrics, bottleneck and environment documentation, not invented performance claims. Avoid performance gains through correctness loss, data staleness, uncontrolled caching or skipped security/restore checks.

1. DEFINITIONS AND INVARIANTS
RCVP means Release Candidate Viable Product, not a prototype or stripped-down MVP. An RCVP app has a real accessible CUI-authored/controlled product interface, usable actual donor-backed functionality, supported file formats, launch/open/create/edit/save/close/reopen/export and relevant playback/rendering, canonical persistent identities, proper permissions, security, error handling, and an authentic build plus interactive smoke and independent RCVP acceptance. ALL applicable baseline functionality from its designated mature donor(s) is available through the running app; donor source merely being downloaded, a placeholder engine or an isolated source test does not qualify. 'Ported to CUI' means present donor features through the canonical CUI user experience and typed adapters while retaining suitable mature donor engines and their capabilities; do not rewrite Firefox/Chromium, LibreOffice, Rnote or other engines in markup. Any unavoidable incompatibility requires an explicit owner-reviewed recorded defect, not a fictional PASS.
RCVP deliberately defers only NEW 9to1-specific enhancements beyond the donor-complete baseline and nonessential expansion features to the later Full stage. Essential Home/CUI/Dulche dependencies, privacy, accessibility, durability, recovery, integration, licensing and security needed for safe real usage are NOT deferrable. Where a browser version is applicable to an app's RCVP, it must also be genuine, usable and backed by canonical providers; an explicitly documented authoritative web exemption (for instance a browser-within-browser exception for Browse) still applies. Track native and browser gates separately.
Full means the complete applicable V2/original/post-release functionality, full approved donor parity, all 9to1-specific extensions, relevant native and web versions, cross-app integration, product quality, and independent requirement-by-requirement acceptance. An app may be RCVP-VERIFIED but not FULL-VERIFIED. Engineering states (WORKING, CHECKPOINT, COMPLETED, VERIFIED, STALLED, BLOCKED) remain distinct from stage/product acceptance. An unexecuted or fixture-only test cannot be counted as full acceptance.

2. PART 1 — FULL CORE PLATFORM + DONOR-COMPLETE RCVP FOUNDATIONS
FULL, including genuine launchable required native AND web counterparts: Dulche (model/inference routing, native tools, Skills, Plugins, MCP, agent/runtime/action/task/permission infrastructure and privacy-safe cross-app memory/context with explicit consent), CUI (complete canonical language, rendering, authoring controls, binding, platform integration and developer tooling), common secure identity/authorisation/storage/application APIs and foundations necessary for Part 1; Home; Spaces (including complete Study/agentic workflows); standalone Assistants, configured Specialists and the shared Agents/Subagents/task-run capabilities; Dev (the FULL development application, not a reduced editor); Files (including its mandatory canonical storage/revisions/permissions/features); and required web versions of Home, Spaces, Assistants, Dev, Files with real login, cloud persistence/sync and shared canonical identity. Shared services needed to make these truly usable are Part 1 FULL even if their separate administrative interface is scheduled later. 'Agents' as a capability and the standalone Assistants/Specialists experiences must not be conflated. Do not substitute a simulated agent for a real workflow.
RCVP in Part 1: Write, Present, Boards, Canvas and Browse. Integrate the declared donor functionality end-to-end via actual engines and CUI interfaces: real word processing, rich presentations and playback, flexible notebooks/boards, drawing, and real web rendering/navigation respectively. Where web counterparts are applicable, ship genuinely useful matching RCVP browser surfaces with canonical identity and persistence; Browse retains its documented web exemption. Advanced original 9to1-only enhancements above those donor-capable baselines are staged for Part 2. The donor baseline is a high standard, not a collection of demonstration buttons.
Part 1 release condition: a routinely launchable Windows/development build, working core apps and real RCVP donor apps, functioning appropriate web routes, live create/edit/save/reopen journeys, meaningful security/recovery evidence and separately recorded independent stage acceptance. Produce and continuously refresh previewable integrated builds DURING Part 1 rather than waiting for every Part 1 item to be independently verified. Label provisional/experimental work truthfully; unverified apps cannot masquerade as release-ready.

6. EXECUTION, SAFE DELEGATION AND VISIBLE BUILDS
Use Part 1 as the primary critical path. Permit safe, independently owned work on later stages in parallel without draining required Part 1 integration resources. Advance each product once an integrated meaningful release checkpoint is achieved; independent full verification continues as a separate gate. Stage dependencies unlock only the minimal required source/API seam, not total completion of every unrelated app. Shared contracts have a single owner and stable API; other workers integrate through documented typed interfaces instead of duplicating stores, runtime or permission brokers.
Current default worker split: Strata/Codex owns Dulche, CUI, common platform, Home, Spaces, Assistants/Specialists/Agents, Dev, Files, relevant Part 1 web/cloud foundations, and Part 1 receiving integration; OpenCode owns the Part 1 RCVP Write/Present/Boards/Canvas/Browse lane and subsequent Part 2/3 application implementations when no active owner conflicts. Existing worker/pr path ownership takes precedence until explicit handoff; never reset or merge dirty, unverified, competing source. Delegate unmentioned applications to the later-app lane by default; delegate OS work to a separately authorised Part 4 lane. Shared Data/Sites functionality has explicit owner handoff before either worker mutates it. Do not begin expensive Part 4 OS rebuilding at the expense of the core release.
Continuous tangible convergence is a mandatory process outcome: maintain an installable/launchable Windows development build and accessible genuine web test deployment as soon as possible; refresh at meaningful validated integration checkpoints. Show all working functionality as it converges rather than requiring users to wait for total release acceptance. Every preview identifies source/artifact SHA, available features, missing functionality, experimental status and supported platform. Do not silently publish externally or incur unapproved expenses. A working demo or source-only unit-test green run is not product acceptance.
Development cycle per vertical user journey: select uncovered acceptance requirement; reuse mature donor and already-tested code; implement the complete actual UI/engine/storage/API workflow; run changed-graph build and focused authentic smoke; integrate reviewed source into the release candidate; independently inspect/accept the exact artifact; continue immediately. Use pinned revision-indexed requirement manifests and incremental inspection; do not reread the entire specification or run exhaustive cross-suite validation on every tiny edit. Run full native/web regressions at significant release and integration gates. Protect security, privacy, permissions, accessibility and data fidelity throughout. Prioritise completed usable journeys per hour over token output, unbounded audits, duplicative test scaffolding or vanity test counts.
Track per application: assigned part; RCVP requirement manifest; Full requirement manifest; explicit donor baseline; owner/branch and source identity; running native/web artifacts; functional smoke; security, persistence and interoperability results; independent RCVP acceptance; independently verified Full acceptance; remaining blockers. Do not report an arbitrary percentage or projected deadline as proof. Claims require evidence. Once every application is Full-verified and 9to1OS Part 4 is Full-verified, the entire plan is complete.

source_text:
Assistants app — current-pass priority
The user-facing Assistants app MUST be implemented and packaged in the current pass. It is an early priority alongside Spaces and Dev so Jacob can use it for authorised 9to1 development work. Give it a named owner within the Spaces/Dev product lane, or explicitly rebalance existing worker capacity. Do not leave app implementation implied by generic agentic-runtime work. Independent app packaging MUST continue in parallel.
Product definition and standalone-app boundary
Assistants is a standalone 9to1 application built as a thin, purpose-built product wrapper over the shared Spaces and agentic runtime. It is NOT a Space inside the Spaces app, MUST NOT be represented as a specially tagged Space, and MUST NOT require the user to enter the normal Spaces app or create/manage a Space in order to create, open or manage an Assistant. Opening Assistants launches the dedicated Assistants product experience; opening an Assistant opens that Assistant's own conversation/work surface.
The wrapper exists to reuse the mature Spaces runtime and achieve close feature parity without duplicating the platform. Assistants SHOULD inherit generally useful Spaces capabilities by default unless a capability genuinely makes no sense for an Assistant. Reuse the same conversation runtime, Task/Run system, model/provider routing, tools, files/project access, memory/context infrastructure, permissions, computer-use implementation, Mini Computer runtime, artifacts, checkpoints, steering, subagents, recovery, generative UI, integrations, persistence, search/research, Dev integration and applicable multimodal capabilities. Do not create a second chat engine, task database, tool framework, permission broker, model router, file/project identity system, computer-use stack or artifact format.
Product category and interaction model
Assistants should belong to the same broad product category as experiences such as Grok-style custom bots, Dots, Muse-style agents and modern workspace/custom agents. This is a behavioural/product-model reference, not an instruction to copy another product's visual design, branding or proprietary implementation.
An Assistant is a persistent, named, user-configured AI identity that the user creates once and returns to repeatedly. It is substantially more than a saved prompt, renamed chat, system-prompt textbox, template, one-off agentic Task, Space or delegated subagent. The same Assistant identity can span multiple conversations, Tasks/Runs, projects, scheduled work, memories/context where permitted, artifacts, checkpoints and applicable Mini Computer state. Starting a new conversation does not create a new Assistant, and delegating a worker does not create another personal Assistant.
The intended experience is: “this is my persistent AI assistant that knows its configured role, can use authorised tools and resources, can continue real work over time, and can proactively help when I have enabled that behaviour” — not “this is a chat with a long system prompt.”
Assistant configuration and identity
Each Assistant MUST have a persistent editable configuration and stable identity. Where applicable the configuration includes name, icon/avatar, description, purpose/role, instructions/personality, preferred model or model policy, reasoning/model-routing preferences, allowed tools, connected apps/services, authorised files/projects/knowledge sources, memory behaviour, computer-use permissions, Mini Computer configuration, Dev/project access, proactive-behaviour settings, notification/check-in preferences, schedules/Automations, voice/multimodal preferences and resource/usage limits. These settings must be exposed through polished product UI rather than relying primarily on raw prompt/config files.
Editing an Assistant's configuration MUST preserve its canonical Assistant identity, appropriate history, valid conversations, Tasks/Runs, memories, permissions and artifacts unless the user explicitly chooses an operation whose documented effect is to remove or reset them. Assistant identity is separate from any individual conversation or task.
Assistants home and conversation experience
The Assistants app MUST provide a dedicated home/library experience for seeing existing Assistants, creating an Assistant, opening recent Assistants, viewing recent conversations/tasks, seeing whether an Assistant is actively working, configuring an Assistant, inspecting its permissions and connected resources, opening current Tasks, managing proactive behaviour, managing its Mini Computer where applicable, and pausing/disabling/archiving/deleting an Assistant as appropriate. Do not redirect this experience into the normal Spaces application's Space list.
An Assistant conversation should expose the power of a modern Spaces conversation through Assistant-focused UI. Where authorised, an Assistant can chat naturally, search/research, use tools, create and edit files, work with 9to1 apps, open Dev, perform durable long-running Tasks, create artifacts, use delegated workers, use computer control, operate a Mini Computer, work across connected services, present generative UI, continue through checkpoints, recover after interruption and accept live steering. The product should expose these capabilities naturally without turning the primary experience into a developer console.
Relationship to Spaces
Spaces remains the general-purpose AI workspace; Assistants is the persistent configured personal-assistant product. They may share underlying components and conversation/work surfaces, but product ownership, navigation, Assistant creation/configuration, identity, proactive controls and Assistant-specific management belong to the standalone Assistants app. Users should not need to understand that Spaces infrastructure powers the Assistant.
The Assistants app requires the applicable shared Spaces/runtime services to be installed or available, but that dependency MUST be handled as a product dependency rather than exposing Assistants as a child object inside the Spaces app. Feature parity should stay close: when Spaces gains a generally useful agentic capability, Assistants should normally gain it through the shared runtime rather than a separate reimplementation.
Proactivity, permissions and Mini Computer
Assistants may support explicitly configured proactive behaviour that ordinary Spaces conversations do not initiate by default, including check-ins, follow-up on unfinished work, scheduled work, configured event responses, continuing persistent tasks, proactive calls and initiating conversations where supported. The user must be able to understand and configure whether the Assistant may initiate contact, which events/schedules permit it, notification channels, resources it may access and which actions require renewed approval.
A general authorisation to be proactive is NOT blanket permission to access unrelated files, accounts, computers, cloud services or projects. Assistant actions remain bound by the canonical permission system and agreed scope. Prior authorisation may cover subsequent actions within that scope but does not authorise unrelated spontaneous actions. Computer use and Mini Computer operation MUST use the canonical permission/runtime contracts and required persistent user notices. An Assistant may have its own Mini Computer VM where configured.
9to1 development workflow
Assistants is an early current-pass priority partly so it can become genuinely useful for continued authorised 9to1 development. A configured development Assistant MUST be able to retain its developer role/instructions, access the authorised canonical 9to1 project, open Dev directly from its Assistant conversation, use the same Files/Spaces/Dev project identity, create or resume the same durable Task/Run, inspect source, make authorised edits, run builds/tests, inspect diagnostics, show genuine diffs, coordinate delegated workers, create checkpoints, survive conversation/app closure and later resume with the same Assistant/project/task state.
Include a real Assistant-initiated development acceptance journey: open the authorised 9to1 project in Dev, perform an approved bounded edit/build/test/diff/checkpoint cycle, steer or pause/resume the task, close and reopen the Assistant/task, and confirm that the same canonical project and Task/Run continue without duplicated state or effects. Exercise denied or revoked access without effects outside the grant. Do not substitute sample repositories, simulated tool responses, disconnected project copies or generic Saved-Agent tests.
The current cloud Astra run remains the primary development environment while available. Making Assistants useful for development does not authorise migrating the active Astra run onto an unfinished Assistants/product harness or transferring its credentials.
Packaging, readiness and completion boundary
Track Assistants explicitly in the app/platform roster and readiness reports with its named owner, source/build identity, applicable Windows/web artifact or deployment, smoke results and outstanding acceptance. Reconcile historical roster totals instead of omitting the app or counting shared framework evidence as app completion.
Do not count Assistants as IMPLEMENTED merely because the Agentic Update runtime exists, Spaces works, Assistant records can be persisted, Saved-Agent tests pass, an Assistant can send text, or a prototype Assistant screen exists. The actual standalone Assistants application and its end-to-end user workflows must exist.
Track Assistants through IMPLEMENTED → PACKAGEABLE → PACKAGED → SMOKE-PASSED → EXTENSIVELY VERIFIED. For Friday packaging, prioritise a genuinely usable Assistants Windows artifact as soon as required Spaces/Dev dependencies permit. Where a web Assistants surface is applicable under the authoritative platform matrix, track and qualify it independently rather than inferring web readiness from Windows.
Smoke verification MUST exercise the actual packaged app, including launch, configured Assistant selection/creation as applicable, genuine conversation, persistence/reopen, shared Spaces-runtime integration, Dev handoff, permissions, at least one genuine authorised development action, steering and clean close/reopen. Extensive verification must then cover the complete Agentic Update contracts, including durable Task/Run persistence, recovery, coordinated workers, Task Dashboard/widget integration, permission enforcement, computer-use notice/control where applicable, Mini Computer operation where applicable, failed-action recovery without duplicated effects, checkpoint/artifact history, correct Assistant identity after restart and supported cross-device/platform behaviour.
The full pulled-forward Assistants and Specialists scope and legacy migration arrangements in 9to1 Post-Release Updates remain mandatory. Specialists remain a distinct configured product type. A generic agent, delegated worker or Assistant does not revive the retired legacy Agents product/API except through the explicitly retained migration/compatibility arrangements.
Agentic Update pull-forward
The Agentic Update defined in 9to1 Post-Release Updates is pulled forward into the current development push and is no longer gated on initial launch. The objective is to establish a production-capable agentic harness early enough that cloud models and eligible local models can execute the same durable work through the same typed app/tool interfaces, checkpoints, permissions, task state and recovery semantics. Cloud quota exhaustion, provider unavailability and equivalent model-routing failures MUST be recoverable routing conditions where an authorised eligible fallback exists. Switching models MUST resume the same canonical Task/Run rather than start a disconnected replacement chat, discard valid checkpoints or lose accepted work.

General Rules
Specification authority
This Google Doc is the canonical authority for 9to1 product behaviour, feature requirements, donor parity, storage rules, UX semantics and unresolved design decisions. Trello is the roadmap/index layer only: product cards MUST remain concise and link to the relevant canonical section rather than duplicate its full specification. If Trello and this document disagree, this document wins unless a later explicit decision explicitly updates the canonical requirement.
Technical specification contract
Normative requirement language
This document is an engineering contract. The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, MAY and OPTIONAL are normative requirement levels, not conversational emphasis.
* MUST / MUST NOT — mandatory for conformance. An implementation that violates the requirement is non-conformant unless this document contains an explicit scoped exception.
* SHOULD / SHOULD NOT — required by default. A deviation is permitted only when a concrete technical constraint makes the requirement unsuitable for that exact case; the implementation MUST record the exception, reason, affected scope, fallback behaviour and validation evidence.
* MAY / OPTIONAL — intentionally optional. Omitting the behaviour is conformant unless another requirement makes it mandatory in a specific context.

Required technical structure for product specifications
Every shipping app, framework and system component MUST eventually define the following information in its canonical section. A section that lacks required fields is incomplete specification, not permission for the implementer to invent behaviour.
* Purpose and boundary — what the component owns, what it explicitly does not own, and which neighbouring component owns excluded responsibilities.
* Authoritative data/state — canonical entities, stable identifiers, ownership, lifecycle states, persistence location, versioning and migration rules.
* Donor/upstream contract — donor repository/source, pinned or selected version policy, licence obligations, required parity surface, allowed replacements and documented exclusions.
* Supported platforms and capability matrix — Windows, 9to1-OS, web and other supported surfaces, including exact differences rather than silent feature loss.
* User-visible operations — exhaustive operations the UI exposes, including create/read/update/delete, import/export, collaboration, recovery, settings and destructive operations.
* Automation/API surface — canonical namespace, action names, argument schemas, result schemas, stable IDs, pagination/streaming where applicable, idempotency semantics, error contracts, permission scopes and risk classification.
* Permissions and security — caller identity, authorisation boundary, high-risk operations, secrets, external side effects, confirmation requirements and audit events.
* Cross-app integration — exact owning app, reference/embed semantics, canonical-object behaviour and how actions route across app boundaries.
* Failure and recovery — expected failures, partial-success behaviour, retry rules, rollback/restore, crash recovery and data-integrity guarantees.
* Performance/resource constraints — limits that affect correctness or UX, including memory/storage/compute ownership where relevant.
* Acceptance criteria — deterministic tests or observable behaviours that prove the requirement is implemented.
* Open decisions — unresolved design questions explicitly labelled OPEN. OPEN items MUST NOT be silently resolved by an implementation agent when the choice could change public behaviour, data compatibility, security or architecture.

State and data invariants
Persistent objects MUST use stable identifiers that do not depend on display names, UI order or mutable paths unless the object is explicitly path-addressed by design. Display names MAY be duplicated unless the product section explicitly requires uniqueness.

source_text: Mutations MUST be atomic at the smallest user-visible operation boundary unless the operation explicitly declares partial-success semantics. When a multi-object operation can partially succeed, the result MUST identify every succeeded, failed, skipped and rolled-back item.

API and error contract
UI and automation MUST call the same domain operations wherever technically possible. An app MUST NOT maintain one hidden behavioural implementation for UI actions and a different incompatible implementation for API actions.

Unspecified behaviour and exceptions
When required behaviour is genuinely unspecified, an implementation agent MUST first determine whether the decision is observable, destructive, security-sensitive, data-format-affecting or architecture-defining. If yes, it MUST preserve existing data/state, avoid irreversible action and record the item as OPEN rather than guessing.

source_text:
Application-level acceptance and anti-substitution contract
APP-AC-001 — Exhaustive scoped manifest. Before implementation/acceptance, map every applicable requirement and donor capability to its app, Part, RCVP/Full stage, platform, real user entry point, owning engine/API, persistence path and verification evidence. Readiness is evaluated against that manifest, not a hand-picked subset of convenient tests. Minimum examples are a floor, not the complete manifest. An absent feature or unexecuted test remains missing/NOT RUN; it is not silently NOT APPLICABLE.
APP-AC-002 — Seven mandatory gates. Each app and substantial user journey must pass Usability; Product fit; Functionality; Integration; Separation and authenticity; User fit; and Refinement. Significant failure of any gate blocks acceptance; a numerical average cannot compensate. Integration includes discoverable navigation, the actual CUI surface, canonical providers and end-to-end artifact flow. Separation and authenticity prohibit developer diagnostics, fixtures and sample success states from impersonating ordinary product behaviour. For interface-free work, record why visual criteria do not apply rather than claim visual testing.
APP-AC-003 — Real product, real artifact. Acceptance launches the actual app/package/route built from the identified source and dependencies, with normal startup, Home/runtime integration and authentic providers. Exercise meaningful multi-step workflows and independently inspect the resulting saved/exported artifact. A parser demo, single text box, disconnected command grid, screenshot mockup, unit-test host or separate demonstration app is never app acceptance. Opening the upstream donor's unadapted UI or external executable is not CUI product integration. Necessary donor engines remain reusable behind typed CUI adapters.
APP-AC-004 — No scope laundering. A working vertical slice is a CHECKPOINT, not an RCVP-complete or Full-complete app. A declared RCVP requires all applicable donor baseline functionality through the real product; new enhancements may be deferred only as the active four-part plan specifies. Existing data, donor behaviours, accessibility, security, durability and essential CUI/user workflows must not be removed to simplify a refactor. Exceptions need explicit owner approval and the scoped evidence required by this specification; an agent-created waiver, hidden menu, disabled command or renamed task does not satisfy the omitted requirement.
APP-AC-005 — Fast prevention before repetition. Establish reusable CUI shell, navigation, toolbar, menu, dialog, inspector and state components. Before repeating a layout across apps, launch one complete representative journey and inspect its hierarchy, work-surface proportions, responsive behaviour and accessibility. Every changed user-facing journey receives focused runtime/visual smoke; shared language/theme/component changes invalidate affected downstream evidence. Reuse unchanged exact-source evidence and cached changed-graph checks; run broader donor/native/web regressions at integration and release gates. Do not impose a whole-suite run or manual approval after every tiny edit, and do not defer all visual review to release.
APP-AC-006 — Independent evidence. A reviewer other than the implementing agent must inspect the exact runnable artifact and independently execute representative workflows, check the exhaustive manifest and challenge product-category and donor-parity gaps. Preserve source/build/artifact hashes, platform, theme/viewport, test steps, observed results, screenshots and representative output artifacts. Source inspection, implementing-agent assertions, fixture-only tests and copied evidence from another build cannot substitute for current relevant runtime evidence. Without an available independent reviewer, record independent acceptance as NOT RUN, not VERIFIED.
APP-AC-007 — Truthful states and blockers. Distinguish engineering status, app RCVP acceptance, app Full acceptance and native/web platform acceptance. Record FAIL, BLOCKED and NOT RUN explicitly. A missing desktop/browser environment is an environmental blocker, not proof of product failure or success. Continue safe unblocked work, but do not report an untested platform or missing mandatory workflow as complete. Tests must not be weakened, skipped or rewritten merely to accept a deficient implementation; update obsolete tests only to enforce the canonical specification and retain regression coverage.
APP-AC-008 — Home and shared-shell rejection cases. Home must present the specified useful dashboard/briefing and app navigation, not an administrator/test panel. Keep tile-management controls in the dedicated Customise experience. Demonstrate normal, offline/local-only, empty and Customise states with real state transitions. Cloud/auth failures remain scoped and actionable; they must not overwhelm or disable unrelated available local workflows. Reject truncated hero/content, malformed grids, duplicate technical errors, inaccessible disabled controls, overlapping AI bars and hidden primary actions. Preserve all specified Home lifecycle, package, permission, account and dashboard functionality; these examples do not replace its complete acceptance manifest.
APP-AC-009 — Screen identity and transition integrity. Acceptance MUST verify that specification-defined distinct experiences exist as actual independently composed, correctly activated views, not just headings or stacked sections in one workspace. For every required launch/home screen, LAUNCH-001–006 are mandatory. The reviewer must inspect the rendered start and working states, real transitions, active commands, focus/accessibility scope and preserved session state in the shipping app. The presence of launch-related labels, separate component files or route declarations is insufficient. A welcome/header/Recent section above the active editor fails even when both sets of controls work. Review other explicitly distinct product experiences for the same flattening defect while preserving intentionally embedded panels, split views, backstage behaviour and shared shell components. Missing visual/runtime evidence remains NOT RUN and must not be promoted to VERIFIED.
Definition of implementation-complete
A component is implementation-complete only when all mandatory behaviour in its canonical section is present and validated. Source code existing, a successful build, a rendered shell, placeholder controls or an API stub do not satisfy a behavioural requirement.

Privacy and data-protection baseline
9to1 MUST apply a platform-wide Privacy Ceiling baseline to every app, framework, cloud service, hosted component, telemetry path, AI feature and operating-system integration that processes personal information. Product teams MUST NOT treat privacy as an app-specific optional enhancement.

source_text: The Privacy Ceiling is derived from the strongest compatible protection required across the supported United States jurisdictions, the United Kingdom and the European Union/EEA, plus deliberate engineering headroom. The implementation MUST maintain a versioned LegalPrivacyProfile describing the currently applicable statutory/regulatory requirements for each supported jurisdiction. Where multiple requirements are compatible, the most protective requirement becomes the global default. Where applicable laws genuinely conflict, the exception MUST be narrowly jurisdiction-scoped, documented, legally reviewed and MUST NOT lower protection for unaffected users or data.

source_text: Engineering headroom means 9to1 SHOULD collect less data, retain it for less time, expose it to fewer systems, process it locally more often and encrypt it more comprehensively than the minimum legally permissible where doing so does not prevent the requested product function. A legal maximum retention period, collection scope or disclosure permission MUST NOT automatically become the product default.

source_text: Privacy by design and by default is mandatory throughout the product lifecycle. New processing purposes MUST NOT silently reuse personal data collected for an unrelated purpose merely because the data is technically available.

Home permission broker
9to1 Home is the central permission broker for app APIs. A caller never dispatches a protected action directly to the target app without Home first resolving its permission state. If Home is not open, 9to1 opens it and shows the approval prompt before the target action executes. A caller may submit the request to the broker, but the requested app action remains PendingApproval until Home grants it.

12. Repository and Environment Authority
Where a canonical repository, workspace, machine, environment, branch, directory, or deployment target has been specified, the agent must treat it as authoritative. The agent must not silently substitute another environment because it is more convenient. Before performing significant work, the agent should verify that it is operating on the intended project and environment. If the authoritative environment is unavailable but useful work can still be carried out elsewhere, the agent must clearly distinguish preparatory work from authoritative implementation and must not falsely claim that the authoritative environment was modified.

21. Donor and Upstream Applications
Where an application or component is based on, forked from, or explicitly uses another application as its donor or upstream implementation, the donor source must be treated as authoritative reference material for inherited functionality. Unless the user explicitly specifies otherwise:
1. The latest appropriate donor source should be obtained or referenced.
2. Existing donor functionality should not be recreated from memory when the actual implementation is available.
3. Relevant features, quality-of-life behaviour, keyboard interactions, menus, workflows, and expected user-facing behaviour should be preserved or appropriately adapted.
4. Proprietary functionality that cannot be reused should be replaced with a project-native equivalent where required rather than leaving an unexplained gap.
5. Required copyright notices, licences, attribution, and source obligations must be respected.
6. The relationship between the derivative implementation and its donor should remain traceable in the project's development records.
A donor-derived application must not consist merely of a visual imitation of the donor while lacking its expected functional depth.

* Donor parity is mandatory. If a 9to1 app is based on a donor application/project, all donor features, user-visible behaviours and quality-of-life improvements must be ported unless technically impossible and explicitly documented. Proprietary donor AI features are the exception: replace them with equivalent 9to1 AI capabilities rather than porting the proprietary AI.
* Deep interoperability is mandatory. 9to1 apps are not independent silos. When a target app declares support for an artifact type, links/embeds MUST reference the canonical underlying document/project/entity rather than create an unmanaged duplicate. Unsupported artifact/app combinations MUST fail explicitly rather than silently flattening, copying or losing functionality.
* Spaces is the conversational editing layer. Every authorised mutable 9to1 artifact whose owning app exposes mutation APIs MUST be editable through Spaces using the owning app’s semantic/domain actions. Read-only artifacts MUST be surfaced as read-only with an explicit reason. Spaces MUST NOT substitute raw UI simulation for an available typed action.
* Automations is ecosystem-wide. Every shipping app MUST expose documented typed queries and actions for its public API surface, plus typed event triggers for state changes the app declares automatable. Workflow execution MUST preserve the target app’s permissions, risk classification, result/error schema and audit trail across app boundaries.
* Cross-app examples are acceptance criteria, not optional demos. Examples include live Canvas pages inside Boards, Files-hosted documents edited from Spaces, Maps routes attached to Planner events, and app-to-app Automation workflows.
* Verification means real behaviour. Source presence or a successful build alone is never enough; parity, interaction, accessibility, platform/package and representative end-to-end journeys must be evidenced.

9to1 V2 — AUTHORITATIVE AMBIGUITY-RESOLUTION AND ACCEPTANCE CONTRACT (11 OCTOBER 2026)
STATUS: Normative, owner-approved clarification. Applies to all applications, CUI, Dulche, RCVP, Full, web and native releases. Supersedes inconsistent older wording on these specific subjects without removing unrelated requirements. No developer or acceptance agent may self-authorise exceptions. The canonical component registry and approved app feature manifests are required implementation artifacts; absence is a blocker, not permission to improvise.

source_text: PARITY-001 — Complete donor functionality. Preserve and make accessible every feature of each version-pinned designated donor, except: (A) third-party paid/subscription/licensed functionality that cannot legally be provided for free; (B) proprietary donor AI surfaces, whose unique permitted capabilities migrate into Dulche and whose duplicated interfaces may be removed; or (C) features irreconcilably conflicting with 9to1's direction after a documented attempt to adapt or replace them (e.g., a fixed traditional animation workflow incompatible with Present's AI/node-based approach). Technical difficulty, rarity, time pressure and developer preference are not exceptions. Prefer equivalent capability through the new experience; UI parity is not required. Each exception needs evidence, classification, impact, proposed preservation/migration/replacement/removal and explicit owner approval. No approval means BLOCKED, not PASS. Maintain per-donor versioned feature inventories with user-visible workflows and test evidence.

source_text: CUI-001 — Exclusive markup and interface ownership. All 9to1 UI markup is canonical CUI. AXAML/XAML and Avalonia native markup MUST NOT parse as CUI, including aliases or silent conversion. CUI owns ALL visible UI: navigation, menus, dialogs, toolbars, context menus, overlays, notifications, settings, controls and specialised-surface UI. Avalonia is permitted only as an internal cross-platform rendering/windowing/input/accessibility infrastructure layer, never a public design language or uncontrolled native-themed interface. Specialised donor engines may compute, render content or perform domain operations behind typed CUI adapters; they may not surface independently styled UI. The canonical versioned CUI component/property registry defines allowed syntax; unknown components/properties fail validation. Native-looking public components and AXAML leakage fail acceptance regardless of functional tests.

source_text: CUI-002 — Conformance gates. Build/CI MUST parse all public UI definitions using the CUI grammar and registry, reject native markup vocabulary and attached-property syntax, inspect runtime UI boundaries, and smoke-test real rendered packaged apps. Valid registered CUI properties must not be rejected merely because their names resemble internal implementation details. Any specialised engine adapter must document lifecycle, content/selection/action contracts, focus/input, accessibility, errors, theme, state and recovery. CUI controls every visible UI affordance, including engine-related context controls. Internal platform primitives are permitted only when visually and behaviourally controlled by CUI.

source_text: DESIGN-001 — Category-derived layout. Before implementing an app, document an evidence-based comparison of 3–5 established applications in its category, including their common workspace hierarchy, navigation, command grouping, tool placement, canvas/document area, properties panels, contextual controls and creation/open workflows. Write/Present/Data should benchmark familiar Docs/Slides/Sheets-style layout conventions, without copying branding or visual design; Picture should compare relevant capabilities of Paint, Photoshop, GIMP and Illustrator, recognising differing target audiences. Derive a shared layout blueprint, document justified deviations and use 9to1's distinct CUI visual identity. Approval tests must examine actual packaged screenshots at representative window sizes, keyboard navigation, density, alignment, hierarchy, overflow and discoverability. Attractive screenshots alone do not establish functionality; functioning controls alone do not establish acceptable design.

source_text: STAGING-001 — RCVP versus Full. RCVP includes all non-exempt donor functionality and everything necessary for genuine everyday use: canonical CUI, launch/create/open/edit/save/close/reopen/export as applicable, accessible navigation, permissions, security, persistence, recovery, error handling, essential integrations and supported formats. Full adds 9to1-specific differentiating enhancements such as generative UI, unless a specific enhancement is explicitly essential to baseline functionality. Every feature is assigned to RCVP or Full in an approved per-app manifest; unassigned necessary features cannot silently be deferred. The four-part delivery order remains unchanged.

source_text: ACCEPT-001 — Real-feature proof. A feature is VERIFIED only when a real user can perform its complete intended workflow in the actual packaged application using genuine engines/providers and persistent state where applicable, with correct results, error handling and reopen/recovery checks. Unit tests, source presence, mock responses, screenshots or disconnected harnesses alone are insufficient. Where a live provider cannot be exercised, report NOT VERIFIED or BLOCKED, never simulate a PASS. Independent acceptance uses the specification and feature inventory, not only implementer-authored tests. Record artifact/build hash, platform, test steps, observed outcomes, screenshots where relevant, defects and reviewer.

source_text: ACCEPT-003 — Security and Dulche privacy. Cross-app personal context is denied by default and shared only following granular, informed, revocable user permission. Encrypt sensitive stored context and protected transfers; minimise data exposed to models and providers. source_text:
CakeUI (CUI)
Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
CakeUI (CUI) is the authoritative 9to1 user-interface framework and .cui is the only final application-markup format for first-party 9to1 applications. CUI is intentionally small, opinionated and quick to learn: ordinary application authors work with a fixed compact element vocabulary, Types, properties, Themes, Definitions, Prefabs, variables, Styles/actions and a small set of structural language constructs rather than an Avalonia-sized public control taxonomy.
CUI is derived from a pinned Avalonia source fork for mature low-level rendering, composition, text measurement, layout foundations, input, focus, accessibility, windowing and platform integration. Avalonia remains an implementation foundation; it is not the public app-authoring framework. CUI MUST compile directly to the CUI/Avalonia runtime representation and MUST NOT translate .cui into AXAML as an intermediate authoring/runtime contract.
Shipping first-party app projects MUST stop recognising .axaml and .hui as accepted application markup. C# and other implementation code remain valid for domain logic, services, specialised controls/renderers and platform integration; ordinary visible application structure and styling are authored through CUI.
CUI-CONF-001 — Public language boundary. A .cui extension alone proves nothing. Shipping authoring registries, schemas, parser/runtime loaders, code generation, hot reload, samples, designer output and documentation MUST expose the canonical CUI vocabulary and typed properties, not donor controls disguised by a file rename. Use Text, not TextBlock; Container Type="Grid", not Grid; Container Type="Vertical Stack" or "Horizontal Stack", not StackPanel. Layout and scrolling use the registered CUI Container properties, including RowSizes, ColumnSizes, Row, Column and independent scrolling, not public RowDefinitions/ColumnDefinitions or Grid.Row-style attached-property syntax. Do not reject valid registered CUI properties merely because a donor has a similarly named property.
CUI-CONF-002 — No permanent legacy aliases. Reject Grid, StackPanel, WrapPanel, ScrollViewer, TextBlock and Border as built-in public element tags, including donor-namespace/reflection escape routes. Border remains a valid registered CUI property, not a primitive tag. Custom (Definition) components remain supported, but MUST NOT be used to re-export the forbidden donor taxonomy as aliases. Import symbol aliases and the explicitly specified CUI shorthand/ID aliases remain valid. An explicit one-time source migration tool may read legacy input and emit canonical CUI with diagnostics; production compilation/loading MUST NOT silently accept or fall back to legacy syntax.
CUI-CONF-003 — Internal donor boundary. Keep the pinned Avalonia fork, its provenance/licensing and required mature low-level capabilities. CUI compiles directly to its own typed representation and runtime binding, never through generated AXAML. Native framework objects, donor-private assets and specialised host implementation code stay behind reviewed renderer/platform adapters; they do not define an alternative first-party application UI. Inventory every first-party shell, page, menu, dialog, popup, inspector and shared component and migrate its ordinary structure/styling to CUI. No generic Object wrapper around an entire legacy app, second hidden UI tree or swallowed parser failure may bypass this boundary.
The framework MUST make common UI concise without becoming ambiguous. Shorthand may reduce typing but MUST NOT change semantics or permit guessing. If a shorthand token has more than one valid resolution, compilation fails and the developer must use an explicit form.
Donor, source and compatibility contract
The implementation MUST obtain and include the selected appropriate Avalonia source revision in the CUI source tree/build graph under the global donor-source contract. The exact upstream repository, selected revision/release, licence obligations and local modifications MUST be traceable.
CUI MUST maintain an upstream-parity manifest for the low-level Avalonia capabilities it relies on and a CUI property-parity manifest for broadly applicable visual/layout/property families derived from Avalonia and mature CSS concepts. A feature being absent from CUI's small primitive element vocabulary is not permission to omit mature framework capability when it can be represented through Type, property, Definition, Prefab or Object hosting.
The public CUI language/runtime is versioned independently from Avalonia. Upstream Avalonia changes MUST be adapted behind CUI contracts and MUST NOT silently alter public CUI syntax or semantics.
CUI-CONF-004 — Authentic specialised surfaces. A registered Object Type may host an actual donor-backed document, canvas, browser or media engine; for example Object Type="WriteDocumentSurface" is a valid integration shape when that Type is registered. Its contract MUST expose the applicable typed content/selection/actions, lifecycle, input/focus, accessibility, theme integration, errors and canonical state. CUI owns surrounding app controls and chrome; the engine owns its specialised content semantics. Neither a static image nor a generic text box is a substitute for a required specialised engine. CUI themes MUST NOT rewrite user-authored document styling or other artifact content.
Core language vocabulary
The built-in visual/structural vocabulary is exactly the ten elements listed below: Page, Container, Text, Image, Audio, Video, Object, Button, Input and Layer. Specialised products extend CUI through registered Type, (Definition), Prefab or Object Type rather than expanding the primitive donor-control taxonomy. Nonvisual/declarative language constructs, including Anchor placement declarations, are separate from these ten elements and retain their specified semantics.
Core visual/structural elements:
* Page — root navigation/render surface and top-level UI scope.
* Container — general layout/composition element; layout behaviour is selected primarily through Type and properties.
* Text — textual content element.
* Image — image content element.
* Audio — audio/media element where a visual/controller surface is required.
* Video — video element.
* Object — host for specialised renderers/objects such as graphs, Canvas surfaces, browser/media/document engines and other non-primitive content.
* Button — standard action control.
* Input — standard input family; Type selects text, number, checkbox, slider and other registered input behaviours.
* Layer — rendering-depth container; Layer is also available as an element property.
