source_text:
The Universal Model Picker is the single shared model/provider selection and routing interface for the 9to1 ecosystem. On Windows/regular 9to1 it is hosted by Home; on 9to1-OS the same canonical state is surfaced by the OS. Apps, Agents and AI surfaces MUST NOT create incompatible private model pickers, provider registries or fallback logic when this shared capability applies.
Compact picker and full manager
The compact picker is used inside apps, Agents and AI surfaces when selecting the effective model/route. The full manager lives in Home/Settings → AI/Models and adds provider configuration, installation/acquisition, aliases, defaults, route ordering, background routing, fallbacks, privacy, resource and lifecycle controls.
Entries expose stable Dulche model identity plus user-facing name/alias, provider/source, local/cloud/remote state, modalities/capabilities, tool/structured-output support, reasoning controls, context/output limits, loading/availability, privacy/residency, entitlement/cost where known and local RAM/VRAM fit where meaningful. Display names are never used as canonical identity.
Simple defaults and capability categories
The normal picker keeps the primary capability configuration approachable: Chat Model/Route, Image Model/Route and Voice Model/Voice. Advanced exposes Audio Model/Route and Video Model/Route. The user may instead choose one Active Model/Route and allow all compatible capabilities to inherit it, with ordered fallback resolving unsupported capabilities.
Chat is the primary general-purpose route for conversation, reasoning, writing, coding, tool use, agentic work and multimodal chat where supported.
Image supports an explicit Inherit from Active/Chat route. Inheritance means use that ordered route and its native image-generation/editing-capable candidates; it MUST NOT silently substitute an unrelated unconfigured image provider. A dedicated Image route is an explicit override.
Voice is the first-class conversational/live-voice selection used by Vision & Voice for supported Conversational, Monologue, Live Listener and Live Translate modes. When the selected Voice Model exposes named voices, the user-facing field is labelled Voice and selects VoiceID while showing VoiceModelID as secondary metadata. When there are no named variants the field remains Voice Model.
Advanced Audio covers dedicated transcription, synthesis, audio understanding/transformation or music/audio generation where applicable. Advanced Video covers video generation, editing/transformation or video-native understanding. These category routes may inherit the Active route or use explicit independent ordered routes.
Active and Background routes
Users may configure a single Active Model/Route for all foreground AI work or assign capability-specific/app/Agent overrides. Separately, a Background Model/Route can be configured for non-interactive work such as background summarisation, indexing/classification, Background Learning processing, permitted Automations AI work, proactive suggestions and other low-priority background tasks.
If no Background route is configured, background work inherits the Active route subject to normal capability/privacy/policy filtering. A task-specific explicit model outranks Agent/app/category defaults; a configured Background route applies only to eligible background work and MUST NOT override an explicit Agent/task requirement.
Ordered Model Routes
Home/Dulche MUST support versioned ordered Model Routes shared by regular 9to1 and 9to1-OS. A Model Route is an ordered list of stable configured model identities plus per-entry enabled/disabled state and routing policy. Users can reorder candidates directly in Home, including by drag/reorder UI, without changing the models' canonical identities.
Example: an Active route may be ChatGPT 6 Sol → Gemma 4 → Fable 5. The ordering means use the highest-priority candidate that is both eligible and available for the request. The router MUST evaluate compatibility before invocation rather than deliberately sending impossible requests to higher entries first.
Foreground and background workloads may use different ordered routes. A user can therefore choose a powerful cloud model first for interactive work while using a small local model first for background work. Users who want simplicity can select a single model and leave fallback entries empty.
Eligibility-first routing
For every routed request Dulche first derives task requirements such as modality/capability, tool use, structured output, context/output requirements, reasoning support and foreground/background role. It then filters candidates against provider/model capability, privacy/locality policy, administrator policy, connection/authentication permission, user fallback policy, entitlement and other hard constraints before considering route priority.
After filtering, Dulche selects the highest-priority available candidate. A lower candidate may be used automatically when a higher candidate is unavailable because of a classified routing condition such as usage/quota exhaustion, provider/model outage, unsupported required capability, context incompatibility, authentication/provider unavailability when another authorised option exists, or local resource insufficiency after permitted reclamation.
Capability mismatch should normally be detected before invocation. For example, if the first two models in a route cannot generate video and the third can, a video-generation request routes directly to the third eligible model rather than failing through the first two.
Conditions that are not model fallback
Model fallback is not a generic retry mechanism. Errors such as missing user files, invalid tool arguments, target-app permission denial, required human approval, business-logic rejection or an external service action failure do not justify silently switching models unless the failure is independently classified as a model/provider-routing condition.
Fallback privacy and control
Each route and candidate can restrict fallback, including no fallback, local-only fallback, cloud-allowed fallback or provider-specific constraints. A route containing cloud candidates does not itself authorise sensitive context to leave the device. Privacy, administrator and task policies are evaluated before route ordering.
A request explicitly pinned to a model with fallback disabled MUST fail transparently rather than silently substitute another model. Likewise a local-only request cannot fall through to cloud merely because the local model is unavailable.
Routing transparency
The effective model and routing reason remain inspectable. Home/Dulche records route identity, selected model and skipped/fallback reasons where relevant, for example 'Sol skipped: usage exhausted; Gemma selected' or 'Sol skipped: video-generation unsupported; Fable selected'. This metadata may be surfaced subtly in normal UI and in more detail through diagnostics/Action Graph without cluttering every response.
Selection inheritance and overrides
The configuration hierarchy MUST be deterministic: request-specific explicit selection → Agent/task override → app/surface override → capability/category route → Background route for eligible background work or Active route for foreground work → configured route fallbacks. A lower-level explicit override wins, while inherited state is visibly distinguishable from an explicit override.
LLM Space and Desktop Space overrides MAY exist but remain scoped. Category overrides are independent; for example an LLM Space may override Chat while inheriting global Image/Voice/Audio/Video routes.
Reasoning and capability validation
The picker renders only reasoning/effort levels actually exposed by the selected model/provider. It MUST NOT invent Low/Medium/High controls for a model that does not support them. Incompatible explicit selections are blocked or clearly explained unless an authorised fallback route can satisfy the requirement.
Aliases and model identity
Users can assign friendly aliases/nicknames to models. Aliases are presentation conveniences and may be duplicated; all routing objects store stable provider-scoped Dulche ModelID values so duplicate names never create ambiguous execution.
Local model lifecycle
Where supported, the full manager provides discover/install or pull, import, verify, download progress, load, unload, remove, update/replace, rollback, storage-location and compatible CPU/GPU/offload configuration. These operations use Dulche Runtime/Den and provider/package APIs rather than a second model-host implementation.
Provider support
Routes may contain compatible local runtimes, configured commercial/cloud providers, self-hosted/OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, another Dulche device, enterprise endpoints and authorised provider/Plugin implementations. Provider authentication and credentials remain owned by the appropriate shared credential/provider system.
Resource awareness
For local candidates the picker may show estimated RAM/VRAM requirement, current availability, loading state and reclaimable resources when known. On 9to1-OS this integrates with the AI-aware resource manager; on other Home platforms it uses the available Dulche/runtime resource information without pretending OS-level reclamation exists where it does not.
Administrator and managed-profile policy
Managed profiles may limit approved models/providers, acquisition, external cloud use, maximum cost/usage class or fallback destinations. Policy filtering happens before user ordering so reordering a blocked provider cannot bypass a School/organisation restriction.
Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
* Regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use one canonical Dulche model catalogue and versioned routing contract.
* Users can use one Active Model for everything compatible or configure separate capability/app/Agent and Background routes.
* Ordered model routing automatically falls through on classified quota, availability, capability, context or resource conditions while respecting privacy, permissions and admin policy.
* Capability mismatch is filtered before invocation where knowable; model fallback is not misused for unrelated tool/app/business-logic failures.
* Users can reorder, enable/disable and inspect route candidates and understand which model ultimately handled a request.
* Voice named variants, Image inheritance, Advanced Audio/Video, reasoning controls, aliases and local-model lifecycle preserve the existing category-specific contracts.

source_text:
Floating compose @ invocation menu
The shared Home-owned floating AI compose component MUST provide one searchable @ invocation menu for Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents and Files. The menu is a single interaction surface with collapsible type sections rather than separate unrelated pickers. Typing @ opens the resource list; typing text after @ filters across all sections while preserving each result's type and identity.
Selecting an item inserts an inline invocation chip/token inside the compose field at the caret position. The rendered token MUST display the resource's icon where available plus its human-readable label, for example an Agent may render as '@[agent icon] John'. The token MUST use a distinct invoked visual state, including colour/style differentiation, while also using non-colour cues for accessibility. Editing/deleting the token removes or changes the invocation rather than leaving invisible hidden attachment state.
Invocation tokens MUST store stable canonical identities, not only display text: Plugin PackageID/version or resolved active version, SkillID/version, AppID, AgentID/DefinitionRevision where required and File/Artifact reference identity/revision or access token as appropriate. Duplicate display names MUST therefore remain unambiguous. The resolved invocation set is included in request metadata, FullLog and Action Graph.
The Plugins section lists Dulche Plugins enabled/available in the current scope; Skills lists eligible Dulche Skills including the built-in Persistent Skill; Agents lists Agents available through Dulche scope resolution; Files searches authorised files/artifacts without silently granting new access. Availability in the picker never grants permission to execute protected actions or read inaccessible content.
The Apps section MUST contain every installed/available first-party 9to1 app plus user-installed applications that 9to1 can classify as safely operable through a typed API/integration or, when separately authorised, Computer Use. App entries MUST expose whether their interaction path is Typed/API, Computer Use Required, or both. Selecting an app whose only route is Computer Use MUST NOT activate Computer Use by itself; the request also requires the explicit @Computer Use invocation.
Game executables and anti-cheat-protected game surfaces MUST be excluded from the operable Apps invocation results even when discovered through Steam, Epic Games Launcher or another launcher/library. If 9to1 cannot confidently distinguish an eligible ordinary application from a game/anti-cheat target, it MUST omit or mark the target unavailable for Computer Use rather than risk automation. Play remains the supported Agent-game route defined by its own contract.
@Computer Use is a reserved first-party system capability entry in the same searchable invocation surface. Selecting it creates the explicit ComputerUseInvocationID required by the Dulche Computer Use contract and makes its active state visible in the compose field before the request is submitted.
Cross-app execution visualisation
Models operating inside any 9to1 app MAY invoke another 9to1 app only when the user's request explicitly names/invokes that app, directly asks for an outcome owned by that app, or unambiguously implies the owning app from the requested artifact/action. For example, 'create a presentation' resolves to Present; 'make a spreadsheet' resolves to Data; an unrelated app MUST NOT be opened merely because the model thinks it might be useful.
Cross-app intent resolution MUST bind to the owning app's stable AppID and typed capability contract. If the required app is not running, Home MAY launch/open it automatically when that is part of fulfilling the request. The target artifact remains canonical in its owning app, and the originating app/Space receives references/status rather than an unmanaged duplicate.
Typed app APIs and shared semantic actions are the normal execution path. Computer Use is not a fallback for missing/failed APIs and remains unavailable unless @Computer Use was explicitly invoked. Permission, review, edit/suggest/view state, conflicts and external-side-effect rules of the target app still apply to cross-app work.
Where an app has a visible editing surface, the user SHOULD be able to watch model-driven edits occur in real time. Home/shared app infrastructure MUST provide an execution-visualisation stream that maps semantic actions to visible UI changes such as objects moving, text appearing, selections changing, slides being created or a virtual cursor hovering over the affected target.
The execution visualiser is representational, not the control mechanism. A virtual cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's real pointer and MUST NOT generate mouse/keyboard input merely to make the animation believable. The canonical typed API/action result remains authoritative; visual animation follows confirmed/provisional semantic events and MUST reconcile to final app state after errors, retries or rollback.
AI conversation presentation settings
Home Settings MUST expose global conversation presentation preferences for Plain text versus Speech bubbles. The preference applies to compatible 9to1 conversational/AI surfaces through the shared renderer rather than each app inventing a different message layout.
User-message alignment and model-message alignment MUST be independently configurable as Left or Right. All four combinations are valid, including both parties on the same side. Alignment changes presentation only and MUST NOT alter message order, authorship, accessibility reading order or exported conversation data.
The selected Dulche thinking-log mode (Precise, Concise, Detailed or Ramble) MUST be configurable in the same AI/conversation settings family. Inline thinking/work regions render beneath or between message text according to chronology; when Speech bubbles are enabled, the thinking/work region visually belongs beneath the relevant model bubble without being styled as ordinary model-authored message text.
Thinking/work presentation MUST use lower visual emphasis than normal chat while remaining readable and accessible. Collapsed 'Thought for ...'/'Worked for ...', ETA status, blockers and Problem events MUST use the same shared renderer across apps so equivalent Runtime state is not represented differently by each product.

source_text:
Home is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
* A native app refuses normal startup when Home is not installed and successfully resumes through the trusted Install Home/bootstrap flow.

* Library opens the same canonical artifact in its owning app rather than creating a duplicate.
* Events preserve typed source records and link to the corresponding Action Graph/entity where applicable.
* Discover aggregates at least two configured model/provider sources without identity collisions and performs a valid install/connect action.
* Universal Model Picker override precedence and fallback policy resolve deterministically and do not cross local-to-cloud boundaries when policy forbids it.
* Permission/trust grants can be inspected, narrowed/revoked/blocked and future calls immediately respect the updated state.
* Mesh pairing establishes stable device identity; capability calls obey both ends’ permissions; device revocation prevents subsequent sync/invocation.
* Home notifications preserve read/dismiss state and typed deep links across restart and OS notification bridging.
* Search/Library results stop exposing content after permission revocation/deletion and indexes can be rebuilt without source-data loss.
* A representative shared productivity object can round-trip across Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces through the Shared Productivity Engine without schema/format loss.
* Account/subscription values shown in Home match the server-authoritative CAKE ID entitlement state and are not inferred from preset labels.
* An app with an incompatible required Home service version is blocked into update/repair instead of running against an undefined interface.
* Home persistent control-plane state can recover from process interruption without silently dropping package activation state, device trust or permission grants.

source_text:
Files is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
* The CUI port accounts for applicable Files/WinUI donor functionality and preserves its core layout/workflows/QoL through a donor-parity manifest.
* 9to1 Drive appears as a normal first-class location and the same FileID opened via web and desktop represents the same canonical hosted object.
* Rename/create/move on one connected client appears live on another client without manual refresh and preserves stable item identity.
* Moving/renaming a file while it is open in its owning app does not break the open document because the app remains attached by FileID.
* Manual Sync now flushes eligible pending operations, retrieves server deltas and reports unresolved errors/conflicts.
* A CloudOnly file hydrates on demand; AvailableOffline works without network; AlwaysAvailable survives restart/cache cleanup.
* Free up space refuses to evict unsynced content and verifies durable cloud revision before eviction.
* Offline structural operations survive device restart and reconcile correctly after reconnect.
* Two conflicting concurrent binary/raw-file edits preserve both revisions or create an explicit conflict; no version is silently lost.
* Two collaborators concurrently reorganising the same hierarchy receive deterministic structural conflict behaviour rather than blind last-write-wins.
* A large resumable upload survives Files/Home restart and continues from validated committed progress.
* A failed transfer integrity check is reported as failure and never as completed.
* Version history and restore preserve later history and identify actor/source/revision.
* Trash/restore/purge behave distinctly and purge uses the elevated destructive flow.
* Sharing/ACL changes propagate to connected clients and revocation prevents future authorised access.
* Creating Write/Present/Data/Board/Canvas artifacts from Files invokes the owning app and creates canonical artifacts.
* Create Stack here/from this folder produces the expected Stack project without duplicating existing source.
* Owning-app real-time collaboration commits durable Files revisions without Files attempting semantic content merges.
* Provider capability differences disable/report unsupported operations rather than pretending support.
* Bulk operations return exact succeeded/failed/skipped outcomes and never silently lose items.
* Private local content is not sent to a cloud AI merely because it is selected in Files.
* Change-feed cursor resume does not require a full filesystem rescan and does not duplicate consequential events.
* Home crash/recovery preserves pending sync journal state and does not create duplicate operations or storage corruption.
* A very large hierarchy can process ordinary incremental changes without complete rescans for each event.

source_text:
Plugins — custom sidebar elements and per-Space visibility
Plugins MUST support contributing custom sidebar elements. An element MUST be able to open an arbitrary configured page/URL, an authorised app surface, an authored CUI page or a generative page, or invoke an Automation or another declared authorised action. Navigation and action-triggering behaviour MUST be explicit. Arbitrary pages remain subject to the existing safe rendering, origin, permissions and external-navigation rules; this capability does not authorise unrestricted code execution.
For each Plugin, the user MUST be able to select which Spaces display its sidebar elements. This selection MUST be inspectable, editable and persisted using stable Plugin, Space and SidebarItem identities. An excluded Space MUST NOT display that Plugin's sidebar contributions merely because the Plugin is installed globally. Sidebar visibility is distinct from permission to execute the Plugin or access Space data; it MUST NOT silently change either.
Attaching a Plugin MUST now be the primary method of supplying custom sidebar elements in custom Spaces. Ordinary Plugin-provided sidebar elements MUST NOT require users to construct a built-in Automation or Space lifecycle graph solely to load the element.
The existing built-in automation/Events & Extensions/full Space graph mechanisms for loading, showing and controlling custom sidebar elements MUST remain supported for enhanced and combined workflows. Plugin and graph routes MUST share the existing sidebar identity, ownership, lifecycle and rendering contracts, preserving AppSurface, CUI and GenerativeUI support. They MUST NOT duplicate the same contribution or replace protected first-party sidebar items. Disabling or detaching a Plugin MUST stop its active contributions without leaving executable orphan actions or deleting unrelated Space content.
Plugin sidebar — supplied concept mockup clarification
The supplied sidebar concept mockup is the applicable visual reference. The relevant example is the My Homework row immediately below New chat and above the divider; the earlier expanded-composer screenshot is not the sidebar reference.
Plugin-contributed sidebar elements MUST support this ordinary navigation-row presentation: an icon on the left, a readable text label beside it, and alignment, spacing and interaction treatment consistent with neighbouring sidebar items. A custom entry can sit directly beneath New Chat within the selected Space's permitted custom-sidebar area; it MUST NOT require opening a separate Plugin panel simply to reach the entry.
The screenshot is a concept reference for the custom entry's presentation and placement, not a requirement to copy its project names, conversation history, colours or complete sidebar structure. Existing protected navigation and Space-scoping requirements remain in force. The Plugin's per-Space visibility selection still determines where its entries appear, and the existing automation/Space-graph route remains supported.
Plugin sidebar API and acceptance
Extend the canonical Plugin and Spaces APIs for contribution registration, configuration, removal, per-Space visibility and authorised action dispatch; UI and API MUST use the same stable SidebarItemID and ownership/lifecycle rules. Test Plugin-defined URL/page, authored CUI, generative-page and Automation actions; persistence after restart; visibility only in selected Spaces; keyboard navigation and accessible names; and safe disable/detach without orphan actions or deletion of unrelated content. The original automation/Events & Extensions/Space-graph contribution route MUST continue to work, including combined workflows without duplicate contributions. The Plugin manifest and Builder MUST expose these contribution contracts rather than creating a second sidebar registry.

source_text:
Spaces is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
* Chat, Study, Tasks, Agent, Shopping, Research, Translate and Experiences remain distinct protected first-party Space types.
* Translate Space shows selected language chips immediately above the normal chatbar, uses normal Space context, and renders each target-language result as its own labelled assistant speech bubble.
* Experiences maintains canonical structured Experience state separately from generated narrative text, including hidden/private state where configured.
* Experience branching/rewind preserves the matching conversation and Experience-state revision without pretending to undo real external side effects.
* Persistent Agent characters receive only their authorised Experience view, while lightweight characters do not require permanent Den Agent creation.
* Experiences can launch a formal Play Match and receive an explicit Play-to-Experiences handoff without implicitly merging MatchState and ExperienceState.
* + New Space creates a user-defined Space and Edit Spaces can reorder/nest/manage Spaces without exposing protected first-party internals.
* The sidebar uses the selected-Space control, built-in destinations, New Chat, Space-relevant options, + New Space and Edit Spaces in the defined hierarchy.
* Stopping a resumable response replaces Stop with Play/Resume and Resume continues the same run without redoing completed consequential actions.
* Editing/regenerating earlier messages creates branches without destroying prior history/action records.
* Every Space inherits globally installed/enabled Dulche Skills/Plugins and available Agents by default, while per-Space exclusions work and do not grant permissions.
* Built-in Spaces expose only the protected Events & Extensions graph and cannot remove/replace required first-party behaviour/UI.
* A built-in Study extension can turn on Do Not Disturb on activation and restore/perform a configured safe action on deactivation.
* A built-in Space can add a custom sidebar item without shadowing/removing protected items.
* Custom sidebar items can host an authorised app surface such as Planner, an authored CUI interface and a safe Generative UI interface.
* User-created Spaces expose the full graph editor with Draft/Validate/Activate behaviour and rollback-capable prior active revision.
* The graph-editor AI bar can create a valid extension graph through typed Node Graph actions and explain the resulting behaviour.
* Invalid type connections, unavailable packages/Agents, missing permissions and unbounded cycles are detected before activation.
* A Write artifact and Board/shared object can be opened/edited canonically from Spaces without duplicate copies.
* Shared Productivity Engine objects round-trip between Spaces and supporting productivity apps without schema/format loss.
* Explicit sources preserve identity/revision/provenance and large source sets use inspectable retrieval/context budgeting.
* A web-disabled/source-only workflow cannot silently browse outside its allowed corpus.
* Persistent Agent permissions are not expanded merely because the Agent is invoked from a Space.
* Private personal Den context does not leak into a shared Space.
* Long-running background-capable work survives navigation/closing the UI and reconnects to Home/Dulche state.
* Action Graph opens the real Dulche execution graph and Subagents remain distinct from persistent Agents.
* Study progress is based on recorded study interactions/answers rather than unsupported confidence inference.
* Tasks remain distinct entities from Agents and Automations.
* Home/Dulche restart preserves durable conversation/run state and does not corrupt Space history.
* Spaces remains usable for ordinary conversation when advanced agentic/tool capabilities are unavailable.
coverage_state: ASSERTION_MAPPING_REQUIRED; candidate scenarios are not proof every clause condition is covered

source_text:
Vision & Voice is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
* Conversational, Monologue, Live Listener and Live Translate operate as distinct modes on shared canonical session/conversation infrastructure.
* Typed text can be submitted during an active Voice session without ending it.
* Conversational Voice supports natural interruption plus explicit pause/mute/end state.
* Monologue preserves outline/progress and can resume after interruption/stopping without restarting completed content/actions.
* Live Listener extracts structured lesson/meeting information while raw ambient audio/transcript is not persisted by default.
* Explicit recording/transcription opt-in is visibly distinct from default Live Listener.
* Live Listener can create authorised notes/homework/date actions and trigger a low-risk contextual app action such as opening Canvas.
* Live Translate supports one-way, bidirectional and more-than-two-language sessions, including simultaneous target captions/output where supported.
* Live Translate uses Dulche Translate for language/glossary/context handling and does not create a second translation engine.
* Live Translate raw audio and ordinary transcript are ephemeral by default unless the user explicitly enables retention.
* Live Translate can use normal Agents/tools and perform authorised translated-context actions only through owning typed APIs and normal approval rules.
* Background/irrelevant speech is not indiscriminately written into notes and uncertain action cues do not silently cause consequential actions.
* Floating voice pill controls the same SessionID as the full app.
* Microphone/output device can hot-switch and device loss produces a recoverable truthful state.
* Voice named-voice selection stores VoiceID separately from VoiceModelID and the UI label becomes Voice when multiple voices exist.
* Discover/Universal Model Picker can recommend/select a compatible high-quality Voice Model without burying Voice under Audio.
* Voice + screenshot, Voice + continuous screen share and camera input work with visible capture state.
* Stopping camera/screen sharing immediately stops delivery of new frames.
* Semantic app context is preferred over screen scraping when available.
* Local-only/privacy policy cannot silently route audio/visual input to cloud.
* Overlay can capture selected context and use typed APIs rather than arbitrary input simulation.
* Overlay can execute an existing Automation using typed selected-text/context input and preserves the Automation's permission/Action Graph contract.
* Continue in Spaces preserves the active conversation/context.
* A high-risk spoken action still requires the correct explicit target-aware confirmation.
* Dictation works in at least Write, Spaces and Mail as non-conversational speech-to-text with Raw/Clean/Polished behaviour.
* Dictation removes filler/false starts in Clean/Polished modes without changing intended meaning and applies supported editing commands through host APIs.
* Home/Dulche restart produces a truthful reconnect/failed state without losing durable conversation state.
* Continuous capture frames remain ephemeral rather than being permanently attached by default.
* Web/native capability differences are reported accurately, including no false claim of OS-global Overlay on web.
* Mic/camera/screen/listening states and all required controls are accessible and not communicated by colour alone.

source_text:
Dulche
Framework role
Dulche is 9-1’s shared llama.cpp-derived local model framework/runtime. One Home-managed Dulche instance serves every 9-1 app through a broker API; apps must never launch their own competing local model servers. It owns model loading, inference lifecycle, resource limits, cancellation and local capability discovery while preserving upstream provenance.
Voice
Voice is a Dulche capability. Dulche owns the audio-session runtime, speech/model lifecycle, streaming, interruption and integration with requests, tools, permissions and logs. The user-facing controls live in Vision & Voice rather than Home.
Voice API
Dulche.Voice();
Entry point to the Dulche Voice subsystem for the caller’s current context.

Agent updates — static and reactive animated icons
Agents MUST support both static image icons and animated avatars. Users MUST be able to choose the presentation for each Agent. The animated-avatar concept is a pet/companion-style icon, using the user's Codex pets/Dots comparison as a design reference, rather than being limited to an unrelated looping image.
Animated avatars MUST react to the Agent's actual activity and relevant conversational events. Required examples include the avatar sitting at a computer and coding while the Agent is coding, and laughing in response to a user joke. Task-state transitions and conversational reactions MUST be configurable and previewable. Reactions are presentation events, not permission grants or claims about hidden reasoning. Animation MUST respect the existing reduced-motion controls and provide a static fallback without losing the Agent's accessible identity or readable activity status.
Agent presentation API and acceptance

Use Den-backed stable identities and versioned configuration shared with AI Studio’s visual builder; presentation changes MUST NOT fork the Agent, alter its permissions or leak private content. Verify saved/reopened configuration, static and animated icons, coding activity, joke/laugh reactions, reduced-motion fallback and readable accessible status, including permission-denied and missing-asset recovery. Connect’s Agent-contact contract supplies email, call and text entry points to these same Agents.

source_text:
Dulche Agents is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
* An Agent created in AI Studio Agent Builder is stored as a canonical Den-backed Dulche Agent and remains usable after AI Studio closes.
* There is no authoritative standalone Agents app or duplicate Agent database.
* Global Agents appear on every compatible 9to1 surface through Dulche scope resolution without being copied.
* Surface-, Space- and Project/Entity-scoped Agents appear only in matching contexts while applicable broader Agents remain available.
* Agent availability does not grant permissions; effective capability resolution narrows correctly across Agent, surface, Space, caller and Home policy.
* Write can expose/use specialist writing Agents with semantic document context, and Vision & Voice can expose/use a Podcast Agent that drives Monologue mode from typed inputs.
* Quick Actions cascade with their Agent, obey context visibility/input schemas and create normal AgentRuns rather than duplicate Agents.
* Default Model inheritance/explicit override resolves through the Universal Model Picker without violating privacy/fallback restrictions.
* Agent memory persists in the correct Den namespace without silently ingesting private/shared-incompatible context or secrets.
* Task → Agent → AgentRun and Automation → AgentRun relationships remain explicit.
* Agent queues preserve provenance, priorities/dependencies and durable state.
* Blocked and Awaiting Approval states remain distinct and recoverable blockers can be handled autonomously where authorised.
* Pause/Stop/Resume/Retry do not replay completed consequential actions.
* Persistent Agent delegation obeys depth/concurrency/budget limits and does not transfer unrestricted parent permissions.
* Persistent Agents and Dulche Subagents remain distinct in API, logs and UI.
* AgentRun Action Graph is the canonical execution graph and outputs open canonical owning entities.
* Home/Dulche restart can recover supported durable runs or reports Cannot recover truthfully without silently restarting work.
* Agent Builder Preview uses the same Dulche semantics while clearly remaining test-scoped.
* Agent Builder/other surfaces perform Agent operations through the canonical Dulche Agent API.

source_text:
Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
Dulche MUST expose a canonical request-aware Tool Registry describing the tools, executable capabilities and usable resources that a model can employ to satisfy a request. The registry is broader than a literal list of function names: it includes first-party 9to1 app actions/APIs, Automations actions, Plugins, MCP tools, callable Agents, Skills that contribute executable workflows through authorised dependencies, Files/resource retrieval, image/audio/video generation capabilities, code/shell tools, web/network tools where permitted and other registered Dulche capabilities. Computer Use is represented only when it has been explicitly invoked under the Computer Use contract.
Every registry entry MUST use stable identity and structured metadata. At minimum it exposes ToolID/CapabilityID, source type and owner, version/revision, human-readable name, action IDs, semantic capability/intent tags, supported input/output types, parameter schemas, prerequisites, permission scopes, side-effect/risk classification, platform/scope constraints, availability/health and whether user approval or additional configuration is currently required. Display name and wording of an action MUST NOT be the sole mechanism used to decide what a tool can do.
Dulche MUST derive an EffectiveCapabilitySet for each request from the canonical registry. The effective set is filtered by the active user/profile, current app/Space/project, installed/enabled package state, app/API availability, explicit @ invocations, platform capability, privacy policy, administrator policy, current permissions/trust and any request-specific restrictions. Installed-but-unavailable, available-but-unapproved and immediately executable capabilities MUST remain distinguishable.
The active model/orchestrator MUST be given an inspectable, context-budget-aware representation of the EffectiveCapabilitySet. Dulche MAY provide a compact high-level catalogue initially and expose query/search APIs for deeper inspection so very large tool inventories do not consume the model's entire context. Capability discovery MUST nevertheless remain available throughout the request and MUST refresh when packages, permissions, target apps or connection state materially change.
Tool selection MUST be intent-based rather than exact-name-based. Dulche MUST translate the user's requested outcome into one or more semantic intents and compare those intents against tool capability metadata, schemas and declared examples/aliases. A tool does not need an action whose literal name matches the user's wording when its underlying capability can satisfy the requested effect.
For example, a request such as 'remind me tomorrow at 4 PM' MUST be resolvable to a time-triggered Automations operation even if no action is literally named CreateReminder. The semantic requirement is a durable time-based trigger that produces the requested notification/action. Likewise, 'create an image of ...' MUST resolve to an eligible image-generation capability such as the first-party image app/tool or an installed authorised image-generation Plugin, even if the tool's action is named Generate, Render, Imagine or another equivalent verb.
Capability resolution MUST support composition. If no single tool can fulfil the complete request but a sequence of authorised capabilities can, Dulche MUST be able to construct a typed ResolutionPlan whose steps pass structured outputs/references between tools. For example, a request to 'create an image and put it on the title slide' may resolve to image generation followed by Present insertion; a request to 'find the file and email it' may resolve to Files search followed by a Mail/Plugin send action, subject to normal permissions and approvals.
ResolutionPlan steps MUST identify the selected ToolID/CapabilityID, action, required arguments, expected outputs, dependencies, permission/approval state and why the step satisfies part of the user's intent. Capability resolution is planning, not execution: selecting a feasible tool MUST NOT bypass its normal permission, approval, confirmation, privacy, cost or side-effect rules.
Before a model states or implies that 9to1 cannot perform a requested digital action, it MUST first perform capability feasibility resolution against the current EffectiveCapabilitySet unless the impossibility is already established by a current authoritative hard constraint. The model MUST NOT answer 'I cannot directly create images', 'I cannot create reminders', 'I cannot access files' or equivalent merely because the base model itself lacks that native capability when Dulche exposes an authorised tool path that can perform it.
A capability that exists but is missing a prerequisite MUST be described as blocked/configuration-required rather than impossible. Examples include ApprovalRequired, PermissionDenied, AccountConnectionRequired, MissingRequiredInput, AppUnavailable, ProviderUnavailable, CapabilityDisabledByPolicy and UnsupportedOnCurrentPlatform. When the missing prerequisite can be resolved within the current request and permission bounds, Dulche SHOULD resolve it or ask only for the specific user decision/input required and then continue.
If several feasible tools can perform the same intent, Dulche MUST select according to explicit user invocation/instruction first, then applicable app ownership/canonical-data rules, privacy/locality policy, capability fitness, permissions, reliability and configured user preferences. Cost/latency MAY participate where policy allows. Dulche MUST NOT choose an unrelated or lower-fidelity tool merely because its action name more closely resembles the user's wording.
Explicit @ invocation remains authoritative. An @Plugin, @App, @Agent, @Skill or other invocation narrows or prioritises the capability source according to that invocation's contract. However, ordinary natural-language requests do NOT require the user to know or name the underlying tool. 'Create a presentation', 'set a reminder', 'generate an image' and similar outcome requests MUST be sufficient for Dulche to discover and use the appropriate capability when one is available.
Skills, Agents and Files participate according to their real semantics rather than being falsely treated as identical callable functions. A Skill may contribute instructions/workflow/tool dependencies; an Agent may be invoked as a delegated execution capability; a File/resource may provide required input/context; an App/Plugin/MCP/native action may perform the mutation. The resolver MUST be able to combine these heterogeneous entries into one plan while preserving their distinct identities, permissions and audit records.
Dulche MUST expose canonical discovery operations equivalent to Dulche.Tool.List(context?), Dulche.Tool.Search(intent, context?), Dulche.Tool.Get(toolID), Dulche.Tool.Resolve(intent, context?) and Dulche.Tool.ExplainResolution(resolutionID). Resolve MUST return either one or more ranked feasible ResolutionPlans or a structured no-feasible-path result containing the evaluated hard constraints and missing prerequisites. Search/Resolve MUST use semantic capability metadata in addition to lexical names.
The Runtime MUST cache capability metadata efficiently but MUST version/invalidate the cache when relevant package versions, app capabilities, connection state, permissions, policy or provider health change. A model MUST NOT continue relying on a stale 'tool unavailable' conclusion after the capability registry has materially changed during the request.
A tool-result or retrieved document MUST NOT be able to self-register new authority merely by claiming that another tool exists or should be allowed. Registry membership and permissions come from trusted Dulche/Home registration, package manifests, app capability contracts and current policy. Semantic discovery MUST therefore improve capability use without creating a prompt-injection route to invented tools or escalated permissions.
Failure to resolve a tool path MUST be truthful and inspectable. Dulche MUST distinguish NoMatchingCapability from MatchingCapabilityUnavailable, MissingPrerequisite, PermissionBlocked and PolicyBlocked. When no feasible path exists, the model MAY explain the limitation, but it MUST NOT fabricate a tool or claim to have performed the action. The Resolution attempt and selected/no-selected candidates MUST be visible in FullLog/Action Graph at an appropriate level of detail.
Acceptance coverage MUST verify at minimum that: a reminder request resolves to an Automations time-based workflow without requiring the phrase 'automation'; an image-generation request invokes an eligible image capability rather than returning a false inability statement; a presentation request can resolve to Present from another app; a multi-tool request produces a dependency-ordered ResolutionPlan; explicit @ invocation overrides automatic source choice; permission/configuration blockers are distinguished from true impossibility; Computer Use does not appear unless explicitly invoked; and removal/disablement of the only matching capability causes a structured no-feasible-path result rather than a fabricated success.

source_text:
Persistent request execution
PersistencePolicy MUST support at least Standard and Persistent. Standard retains the ordinary Runtime finish/timeout/checkpoint behaviour defined elsewhere. Persistent is a durable root-request policy intended for work that should continue until its user-visible completion predicate has been satisfied.
A Persistent request MUST define or derive an inspectable CompletionContract from the user's request, active Skill requirements and target-app acceptance criteria. Completed is valid only when required outputs exist, required validation/verification has run where applicable, required target mutations are confirmed and no required work item remains Pending, Running, Retryable or Blocked. A checkpoint, partial deliverable, progress report or model statement such as 'done' is not itself completion evidence.
Soft request duration limits, provider execution leases and internal scheduling slices MUST NOT terminate a Persistent request merely because a continuation boundary was reached. When continued execution requires a new model invocation, endpoint lease or recovered process, Dulche MUST create a linked attempt under the same RootRequestID, restore the latest safe state/checkpoint and continue. Completed consequential actions MUST be reconciled before retry so persistence does not duplicate side effects.
Persistent requests MUST remain cancellable. Pressing the user-visible Stop control targets the root persistent request, requests safe-boundary cancellation of unfinished dependent work and produces the normal Cancelled result with retained partial output/logs. Persistence MUST NOT reinterpret an explicit user Stop as a transient interruption to auto-resume.
While a Persistent root request is active, ordinary user messages sent through the same compose surface are SteeringMessages belonging to that root request. They are appended durably, ordered by receipt sequence and presented to the orchestrator at the next safe planning boundary without terminating the current turn. They MUST NOT be implemented as ReplacePrompt or StopResponse, and MUST NOT cause already completed actions to replay.
Persistent orchestration MUST maintain a dependency-aware work graph. A structured Blocker marks only the work nodes that depend on it. When a blocker needs user action or permission that the agent cannot obtain itself, Dulche surfaces the blocker and continues every runnable node that does not depend on it. If all remaining nodes are blocked, the root state becomes AwaitingUser; AwaitingUser is non-terminal and keeps recovery/checkpoint state until the user resolves, changes or explicitly stops the task.
Budgets, administrator policy, permission boundaries and hard safety restrictions still apply. Persistence MUST NOT convert a denied action into an allowed action or silently purchase/consume resources beyond configured policy. A limit that can be changed by the user becomes a structured blocker; a hard non-overridable policy restriction remains recorded truthfully and the request continues any unaffected work.
Persistent state MUST survive supported Home/Dulche restarts. Den MUST retain RootRequestID, request revision, CompletionContract, task/dependency state, SteeringMessages, blockers, checkpoints, completed side-effect evidence, active Skill versions and attempt lineage required to resume without fabricating progress or repeating consequential work.
Context compaction and Context Summarisation
Context compaction is a first-class Dulche Runtime capability, not an app-specific prompt trick. Dulche MUST track the effective context budget for every model invocation and MAY initiate automatic compaction before hard exhaustion using model/provider-specific safety margins. Apps and Agents consume the same canonical compacted session state rather than implementing incompatible private compaction.
Compaction MUST preserve semantic obligations required to continue the task: current user instructions and constraints, active permissions/trust decisions, CompletionContract, outstanding tasks and blockers, accepted decisions, stable object/file/artifact IDs, current revisions, completed consequential actions, verification evidence, relevant source provenance and any exact values whose precision is required. Redundant conversational phrasing, duplicated status chatter and obsolete intermediate reasoning MAY be reduced.
Compaction MUST be non-destructive to durable history. The original authorised conversation, tool records and artifacts remain in Den according to retention policy; the compacted context is a derived execution view with provenance back to source message/event ranges. A model MUST NOT be told that omitted content never existed merely because it is outside the active compacted view.
If ordinary compaction cannot create enough safe context without materially losing required information or required media fidelity, Dulche MUST transition to Context Summarisation rather than silently dropping required content or returning ContextExceeded immediately. Typical triggers include a conversation dominated by images/media that cannot be reduced further without unacceptable information loss, unusually dense tool history, or a model whose effective context limit is smaller than the preserved minimum working set.
Context Summarisation is a distinct Dulche job. A summariser model reads the retained conversation/history section by section using bounded windows so the summariser's own context cannot overflow. Each section produces a structured intermediate summary containing obligations, facts, decisions, identifiers, artifacts/references, completed actions, unresolved work/blockers, provenance and continuity notes. Dulche then performs one or more bounded merge passes until a final execution summary fits the target context budget.
Section boundaries MUST be deterministic and provenance-preserving. A merge MUST NOT discard a requirement merely because it appears only once. Conflicting instructions or facts MUST remain represented as a conflict with source references instead of being flattened into an invented resolution. Exact code, identifiers, numeric values, legal/technical constraints or other precision-sensitive content that cannot be safely paraphrased MUST remain as pinned excerpts or stable references rather than approximate prose.
Images, audio, video and other large artifacts SHOULD remain out-of-band as stable artifact references wherever the target model can retrieve them on demand. Context Summarisation MAY summarise authorised derived observations/metadata, but MUST NOT claim that visual or media detail was preserved if the summariser could not inspect it. Required uninspectable media remains a blocker or retained reference, not fabricated text.
A local summariser model MAY be used automatically when an eligible local model is available under the configured routing/policy. Sending conversation content to a cloud summariser requires explicit user permission for cloud Context Summarisation or an existing user setting that clearly grants that permission for the relevant scope. A cloud-capable model in an ordinary fallback route does not by itself grant permission to upload context for summarisation.
If cloud summarisation is required to continue, permission is absent and no eligible local summariser can satisfy the job, Dulche MUST surface ContextSummarisationPermissionRequired/ContextCapacityBlocked as a non-destructive blocker. Persistent requests enter or remain AwaitingUser as necessary rather than losing history or pretending the task completed.
Dulche MUST expose canonical operations equivalent to Dulche.Context.Compact(sessionID, options?), Dulche.Context.Summarise(sessionID, options?) and Dulche.Context.GetState(sessionID). Results MUST report source ranges/revisions, target model/context limit, method, summariser ModelID when used, retained pinned items, omitted/referenced artifacts, token estimates where available and whether the resulting context is sufficient for the next invocation.
Computer Use
Computer Use is a first-class Dulche capability but MUST be opt-in per request. It is enabled only by an explicit @Computer Use invocation token or an equivalent explicit user control that resolves to the same ComputerUseInvocationID. An ordinary natural-language request, an @App mention or failure of a typed app API MUST NOT silently activate Computer Use.
The Computer Use capability may control eligible graphical applications through supported pointer, keyboard, accessibility/automation and visual-interaction primitives. It SHOULD use the fastest reliable state channel available, including accessibility/automation metadata where appropriate, avoid unnecessary human-speed delays, batch safe independent interactions where supported and verify state transitions instead of relying on fixed sleeps. Speed MUST NOT weaken verification or permission gates.
By default, the first attempted interaction with each target application in a Computer Use run requires user approval for that AppID/process identity, and changes to application or operating-system settings require approval before mutation. Home settings MUST allow the user to change this policy to automatic approval for eligible apps and to an Approve All eligible-apps policy. Persisted approval policy remains scoped by user/profile, app identity and the normal Home trust/permission model.
Auto-approve and Approve All MUST NOT bypass hard exclusions, administrator policy, OS security boundaries or other non-overridable safeguards. Computer Use receives no more filesystem, network, credential, settings or app authority than the invoking user/request already possesses.
Generic Computer Use MUST NOT attach to, send input to, automate or manipulate game executables or anti-cheat-protected game surfaces, including games launched or managed through platforms such as Steam or Epic Games Launcher. When classification is uncertain and anti-cheat/game automation risk is plausible, the target is ineligible by default. This exclusion exists independently of user trust level because generic automation can create account/anti-cheat risk.
The game exclusion does not prohibit Dulche Agents from participating in games deliberately configured through the 9to1 Play framework. Play interaction MUST occur through Play's typed GameDefinition/Match/contestant actions and capability isolation, not by using generic Computer Use to drive an external game client.
Every Computer Use run MUST produce an inspectable action stream with target app/window identity, action type, timestamps, relevant pre/post state evidence, approvals, failures and side effects. Sensitive screen regions, credentials and typed secrets MUST follow the normal redaction and permission rules; logs MUST NOT become a second plaintext credential store.
Dulche Autoreview MUST inspect proposed and recent Computer Use actions continuously. It MUST flag patterns including repeated identical or near-identical actions without progress, repeated failing commands, oscillation between states, privilege escalation, bulk/destructive deletion, destructive shell commands such as rm -rf or platform equivalents, security-setting changes, suspicious executable/download flows and other high-risk sequences. High-confidence imminent destructive risk MUST be able to pause the next action for review rather than merely add a passive warning.
Autoreview findings are structured ProblemEvents and MUST feed the shared Problem handling contract. A Computer Use recovery intervention MUST preserve the current request, state and logs and SHOULD redirect to a safer or more direct interaction strategy. It MUST NOT hide that a risky action was proposed or attempted.
Thinking logs, work state and ETA
Thinking-log presentation is a first-class Dulche feature backed by Runtime events. Home MUST expose one global user preference with the modes Precise, Concise, Detailed and Ramble; compatible apps inherit it unless an explicitly supported per-surface override exists. If no preference has been set, Precise is the default.
Precise shows only thinking/work events that materially advance the task, such as a resolved decision, discovered blocker, completed verification step or changed plan. It MUST suppress repetitive self-talk and events that do not change task state.
Concise renders short activity summaries suitable for rapid scanning, for example 'Moving a square', 'Opening Browse', 'Checking the build' or 'Waiting for approval'. These summaries MAY be generated from richer telemetry but MUST remain faithful to the underlying action/state.
Detailed exposes substantially more model/provider-permitted reasoning trace and task rationale, including intermediate decisions and why a strategy changed when that information is actually available and permitted. It MUST still distinguish observed facts, tool results, summaries and model reasoning.
Ramble exposes the maximum provider/model-permitted thinking/work trace available to Dulche, including abandoned approaches, self-corrections and changes of mind when the provider actually supplies those events. Ramble MUST NOT reconstruct, infer or falsely label undisclosed private chain-of-thought as if it had been exposed by the model/provider.
Thinking mode changes presentation only. It MUST NOT change the model's configured reasoning effort, tool permissions, stored audit truth, Action Graph or provider privacy rules. Provider-unavailable thinking remains Na/Unavailable under the existing Result contract.
While active, permitted thinking/work events render inline in chronological position with the conversation rather than in a separate hidden console. The visual treatment MUST be lower-emphasis/ghost-like relative to user/model message text while still meeting accessibility contrast requirements and MUST use non-colour cues so users can distinguish message content from thinking/work content.
When the active thinking/work phase ends, the inline region collapses under a disclosure labelled 'Thought for <duration>' when no tool/action execution occurred, or 'Worked for <duration>' when one or more tools/actions were executed. Duration uses the Runtime's active execution span for that phase rather than queue time. Expanding the disclosure restores the permitted events according to the selected display mode.
After 60 seconds of continuous active execution in one foreground 9to1 turn, Dulche MUST request an ETA from the active orchestrating model through a canonical ETA request. The model returns an estimated completion timestamp plus optional confidence/reason. The UI displays the timestamp in the user's locale/time zone and clearly marks it as an estimate, not a guarantee. Paused/AwaitingUser time does not count as continuous active execution.
Dulche MUST expose an operation equivalent to Dulche.RequestETA(requestID). An ETA response includes RequestID, AttemptID, EstimatedCompletionAt, GeneratedAt and optional Confidence/Reason. If the active model cannot provide a meaningful estimate, the result is explicitly unavailable; Dulche MUST NOT invent a timestamp. Material replanning MAY request an updated ETA and MUST replace rather than stack stale estimates in the primary UI.
Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
Problem handling is a first-class Dulche Runtime capability for detecting, surfacing and recovering from common model/agent failure modes without forcing every app to implement its own ad-hoc watchdog.
The canonical ProblemType set MUST support at least Looping, NoProgress/Stuck, Repetition, HallucinationOrFabrication, OverAgreement/Sycophancy, InstructionDrift, ContradictionWithGroundedState, RepeatedToolFailure, UnsafeActionPattern and Other/UserReported. Additional typed categories MAY be added versionably without collapsing distinct existing meanings.
Loop detection MUST consider semantic and action-level repetition, not only identical text. Examples include repeatedly issuing the same failing command, alternately undoing/reapplying the same mutation, reopening the same surface without new evidence, recreating completed work or repeatedly restating the same answer while the task remains unfinished.
Hallucination/fabrication detection SHOULD use available grounded evidence such as tool results, canonical app state, source provenance, stable object IDs and completion evidence. Dulche MUST flag fabricated claims of completed actions, nonexistent files/entities/tool results or unsupported factual assertions when confidence is sufficient; it MUST NOT treat disagreement with an unverified model statement as proof that the user is wrong.
OverAgreement/Sycophancy detection SHOULD flag responses that materially adopt or endorse a user's factual premise, conclusion or requested assessment without adequate evidence when the task calls for grounded evaluation. Recovery prompts the model to re-evaluate the evidence and user request; it MUST NOT mechanically disagree with the user merely to appear independent.
When automatic detection reaches its configured intervention threshold, Dulche creates a ProblemEvent and injects a clearly identified Runtime recovery directive at the next safe boundary. The directive tells the model what failure pattern was detected, relevant evidence and the required correction, such as stop repeating the command, reassess grounded state, use a different strategy or verify the claimed result. Runtime recovery directives MUST NOT be forged as user-authored messages.
If the detected problem is associated with a proposed consequential or dangerous tool/Computer Use action, Dulche MAY pause dispatch before the action and require re-planning or applicable approval. Lower-risk reasoning-quality problems SHOULD normally correct the active request without cancelling the turn or discarding valid completed work.
Every conversational 9to1 AI surface MUST expose a small Problem pill above/adjacent to the compose bar. The user can invoke it even when automatic detection did not fire, select a ProblemType and optionally add a note. Manual reports enter the same ProblemEvent/recovery pipeline and are delivered to the active request at a safe boundary without implicitly stopping the request.
ProblemEvents MUST record stable ProblemEventID, RequestID/AttemptID, category, detector source (automatic, autoreview or user), timestamp, safe evidence references, confidence when machine-detected, intervention taken, affected action/node and resolution outcome. They MUST appear in FullLog/Action Graph with sensitive content redacted as required.
Problem detection MUST itself be bounded and loop-safe. A false-positive recovery that does not improve state MUST NOT trigger an endless reviewer/model ping-pong. Repeated unresolved problems should escalate to a visible blocker, alternate model/strategy where permitted, or user decision while preserving completed work.
Dulche Den
Purpose
Dulche Den is Dulche's persistent, cross-harness storage standard. It allows Dulche state to remain available across compatible apps and harnesses rather than being tied to one running endpoint or one application session.

source_text:
Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
DEN-PRIV-001 — Encryption: Den personal data, including memory, context, conversations, embeddings, indexes, journals, attachments, backups and snapshots, MUST use authenticated encryption at rest. Keys MUST be held in an OS-backed secure key store or equivalent, never hardcoded or logged. Exports MUST be encrypted by default; authorised plaintext export requires explicit informed confirmation.
DEN-PRIV-002 — Opt-in continuity: Cross-app, cross-Agent, cross-harness, cross-device and cross-provider access to Den personal context MUST be disabled by default. Each additional scope requires explicit, granular, informed user consent. Installing an app, signing in, selecting a model or enabling Den persistence MUST NOT silently enable sharing.
DEN-PRIV-003 — App permissions: Every consuming app, Agent, Assistant, Plugin, MCP, connector or tool MUST receive explicit, scoped user authorisation to request personal Den context. Grants MUST distinguish read, write, create-memory, cross-app reuse and share/export as relevant; show recipient, purpose, scope and expiry; support inspection, revocation and deletion. Apps cannot acquire broader privileges through another app or an AI model.
DEN-PRIV-004 — Model-only semantic access: Personal Den content may be disclosed only as minimum-necessary context directly to the explicitly authorised model inference request through the trusted Dulche broker, and NOT as raw data to other application APIs, Plugins, MCPs, tools, telemetry, analytics, arbitrary app code or external services. Broker-side permission and data-minimisation checks MUST enforce this boundary. Model access is not a general permission to export data. Cloud inference requires separate explicit consent describing the third-party processor; no covert fallback from local to cloud.
DEN-PRIV-005 — No onward disclosure: Models/Agents MUST be instructed not to quote, forward, paraphrase, embed in tool arguments or otherwise relay protected Den content to other app components, tools, APIs, third parties, other users or recipients without specific user authorisation. Crucially, instructions alone are insufficient: Dulche MUST enforce tool-input/output and action-argument information-flow restrictions and deny unapproved onward transmission. Sensitive context must not be exposed in generated UI, logs, traces or diagnostics by default.
DEN-PRIV-006 — User control: Users MUST be able to see which apps/models can access which Den scopes, view why data was used, grant and revoke access, selectively forget/delete entries and disable cross-app continuity without disabling all local functionality. Consent must be separate from a generic terms-of-service agreement; changes to access scope require renewed consent.
DEN-PRIV-007 — Lifecycle and security: Encrypt data in transit where applicable, minimise plaintext lifetime in memory, protect against prompt injection and confused-deputy privilege escalation, segregate personal/team/app namespaces, define retention and secure deletion, and ensure exports/imports, synchronisation, backups and recovery preserve permissions. Protect secrets independently from Den memory.
DEN-PRIV-008 — Acceptance: Tests MUST verify default-deny cross-app isolation, per-app prompts and revocation, encrypted on-disk files/backups, prohibited tool/API exfiltration, prompt-injection resistance, cloud-provider opt-in, permission-aware retrieval, and correct behaviour when permissions change mid-run. Failing any security gate blocks acceptance. This privacy contract takes precedence over any earlier Den wording that could imply automatic cross-app availability.
Storage structure and portability
Den is a directory-based persistent store with a versioned den.json manifest, structured records, a transaction journal and separately stored or referenced large objects. Portable records use UTF-8 JSON; local databases and indexes may accelerate access but must not be the only readable copy or create an incompatible private format. Exports contain authorised records and explicitly selected attachments. Reference model weights and external Files documents by identity/content hash rather than copying them by default. No special bundle extension is mandated.

source_text:
Persistent Memory
Persistent Memory is a core Dulche Den subsystem for durable cross-session information about the user, recurring entities, preferences, decisions, projects and other scoped context that Dulche should be able to retrieve in future conversations or authorised surfaces. It is separate from Background Learning.
Memory is not one opaque prompt file. A persistent MemoryEntry should carry stable identity, content or structured value, subject/entity, memory type/category, scope, source/provenance, confidence where applicable, created/updated state, supersession/correction relationships, retention state and user-edited/locked state where supported.
Scopes
Memory can be scoped so unrelated Agents/apps do not receive unnecessary context. Supported scopes should include global/user memory plus narrower project, Agent, app/surface or other explicit contexts where appropriate. Retrieval MUST respect both scope and permission.
Creation and retrieval
Dulche may create or update memories from eligible conversations/context according to the user's Memory Frequency and memory policy. Retrieval is relevance-based: only memories useful to the active request/context should be injected, rather than the complete memory store.
Explicit user corrections supersede contradictory earlier memories. Den MUST retain enough provenance/revision information to distinguish an explicit user statement from an inference and to avoid repeatedly resurfacing a memory that has been corrected, superseded or deleted.
Memory Frequency
Settings MUST expose a Memory Frequency preference with exactly four user-facing levels: Never, Sometimes, Often and Always. The selected level controls how readily Dulche autonomously creates, reinforces or updates Persistent Memory from eligible non-temporary interactions.
* Never: Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, reinforce or update Persistent Memory from ordinary interactions. Direct user-invoked memory-management actions are separate explicit operations.
* Sometimes: use a conservative threshold and retain only clearly durable, repeatedly useful or high-value information.
* Often: use a lower threshold and remember useful preferences, decisions, entities and ongoing context more readily when they are likely to help future responses.
* Always: evaluate every eligible interaction for durable memory and normally retain information that satisfies the memory policy, while still deduplicating noise, respecting scope/retention rules and avoiding ineligible information.
Changing Memory Frequency affects future autonomous memory behaviour; it MUST NOT silently delete existing memories. The setting is independent of Background Learning.
Temporary chats in Spaces
Spaces can provide Temporary Chats. Persistent Memory creation is disabled inside a Temporary Chat regardless of the user's Memory Frequency. While a chat is temporary, Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, update, reinforce, merge or promote Persistent Memory from that conversation.
Any explicit action that would save new Persistent Memory from a Temporary Chat must be unavailable or clearly report that memory creation is disabled for temporary chats. Temporary-chat memory-write suppression MUST NOT be bypassed by an Agent, plugin, Skill, tool or Background Learning pipeline.
This rule governs memory creation/writes. Whether existing authorised memories are retrieved into a temporary chat is a separate context/privacy policy and MUST NOT be inferred from the memory-write prohibition.
Management and lifecycle
Users must be able to inspect, search, edit/correct, supersede and delete persistent memories through the appropriate settings/Den surfaces. Deletion and retention use Den's normal lifecycle, sync and purge contracts. Memory export/import must preserve scopes, provenance and deletion/supersession semantics rather than flattening entries into plain prose.
Persistent Memory acceptance requirements
* Persistent Memory exists as a distinct Den record system and is not substituted by Background Learning, session context or Agent-only memory.
* Memory retrieval is relevance-, scope- and permission-aware.
* Never/Sometimes/Often/Always control autonomous memory creation/reinforcement with the semantics above.
* Temporary Chats in Spaces cannot create, update or reinforce Persistent Memory regardless of frequency or calling surface.
* Corrections/supersession are durable and user-manageable, and explicit user statements remain distinguishable from inference.
Permissions and secrets
Authorise access per principal, namespace and object/action. Reading context, modifying an agent, executing tools and administering Den are separate permissions enforced below the UI. Revocation applies to future reads/searches/executions; it does not erase copies already disclosed.
