source_text:
Routing and route planning
Maps MUST support route planning for driving, walking, cycling and public transport where the active providers/data support those modes, with typed extension points for additional modes. Routes contain structured legs/steps, provider provenance, travel-mode information, timing/freshness where applicable and sufficient geometry for rendering/navigation.
A route can be referenced, embedded, shared and manipulated by other 9to1 apps. A route is not reduced to copied text directions. Alternative routes and provider uncertainty/freshness remain available where supported.
Normal route building in Search mode MUST allow selecting an origin/destination, adding intermediate places, reordering/removing stops and editing route preferences without invoking AI.
Saved custom routes / Custom Journeys
Users MUST be able to build, name, save, edit, duplicate, share and later start reusable custom routes/journeys. A custom route can describe both where the user travels and what the user intends to do along the way; it is richer than a simple list of waypoints.
A SavedRoute/CustomJourney must support ordered typed steps such as TravelStep, StopStep, WaitStep, ActivityStep and ManualInstructionStep or equivalent. Examples include walk to a coordinate, sit on a named bench, wait ten minutes, grab coffee from a selected place, use a shortcut, take a particular entrance, then continue to college.
Each step may include a canonical Place/Landmark/Coordinate reference, transport mode, optional timing or stop duration, notes, routing preferences and required/preferred/optional semantics. These semantics allow dynamic rerouting to adapt ordinary travel segments without silently removing user-authored intent.
Users may create user-defined path segments that are not present in provider routing graphs, for example a campus cut-through, alley, informal footpath or other personally known shortcut. Such segments MUST be visibly marked as user-defined/unverified by provider routing data and MUST NOT be presented as provider-validated infrastructure.
AI mode can create and edit SavedRoutes from natural language, for example: 'Create my Walk to College route: walk to the bench by the river, sit there for ten minutes, grab coffee from Z, take the shortcut behind the library, then turn right to college.' Dulche resolves real referenced entities where possible and must present ambiguity rather than hallucinating a landmark.
During active navigation, non-travel steps such as 'sit on Riverside Bench for 5 minutes' or 'grab coffee' are valid current journey steps. The route can continue after the user marks/completes/skips the step according to the journey model.
Saved custom routes can be shared with other users where permissions allow, preserving route geometry, user-defined instructions, typed stops and shared/community landmark references. Private landmark details must not be leaked merely because a route is shared; sharing semantics must explicitly handle private dependencies.
Navigation to arbitrary/custom destinations
Any canonical Place, PersonalLandmark, CommunityPOI or raw permitted coordinate can be a navigation destination even when no street address exists. Routing SHOULD bring the user to the closest supported route-graph point and then represent the actual final coordinate honestly rather than inventing a road/entrance.
Custom/community destinations must participate in navigation, route sharing, Planner/Event references and Dulche requests just like provider-defined places, while retaining provenance and verification status.
Live information and dynamic routing
Where providers support it, Maps can expose live traffic, incidents, road closures, transit departures/delays and dynamic journey times. Live-looking information MUST retain provider provenance and freshness timestamps/state. Stale data MUST NOT be represented as current.
Saved/custom journeys may be dynamically rerouted around disruptions while preserving required user-authored stops/instructions where feasible. If a required custom/user-defined segment cannot be validated or becomes impractical, Maps must surface the conflict rather than silently deleting that instruction.
Location permissions and privacy
Location data is sensitive. Maps/Home permissions MUST distinguish at least resolving a known PlaceID, searching places, approximate current location, precise current location and background location. Location history, if implemented, requires a separately explicit capability/retention model.
An app does not automatically receive the user's live location merely because it can call Maps APIs. Dulche natural-language requests are subject to the same location permissions; 'near me' and routing requests cannot bypass precise-location controls.
Search history, route history, precise locations, Home/Work-style places, saved routes and private landmarks require user-visible retention/clear controls. Sensitive location history MUST NOT automatically become globally indexed Go content or extension-readable data.
Offline operation
Maps MUST retain mature CoMaps-derived offline capability and support downloadable regions where data/provider licences permit. Offline mode should support map rendering and, where the retained/local datasets allow it, place search/geocoding and routing without requiring a live cloud service.
Downloaded region management must show storage usage, version/freshness and update state. Licence/provider rules govern whether particular imagery/tiles/datasets may be cached or redistributed; unsupported offline caching MUST fail explicitly rather than silently violating provider terms.
CUI embeds and cross-app composition
Maps is both a full app and a CUI surface provider. It MUST expose reusable typed CUI components such as PlaceCard, MapView/MiniMap, LocationPicker, RouteCard and Journey/Navigation surfaces so other 9to1 apps can embed real Maps functionality without cloning it.
Planner/Events can attach canonical Places/Routes; Boards and Spaces can embed interactive Place/Map cards; Write/Present can insert linked map/place/route objects; Forms can use the canonical LocationPicker; Automations can reference place/location conditions subject to permissions.
Maps MUST be available as the real native surface through 9to1://Maps and support typed deep links to canonical place/route/journey objects. It therefore participates naturally in Browse tabs and Split View, for example Maps beside Planner or Write beside a route.
Dulche integration
Dulche accesses Maps through typed semantic capabilities, not map-pixel scraping. Capabilities can include SearchPlaces, ResolvePlace, GetCurrentLocation, BuildRoute, ModifyRoute, SearchCommunityPOIs, CreateLandmark, CreateSavedRoute, AddRouteStep and StartNavigation subject to the appropriate permission/action policy.
Natural-language context such as 'near me', 'near college', 'between here and home', 'along this route', 'around that place' or 'the restaurant I just looked at' must resolve against real permitted Maps state: current location, SavedPlaces, selected Places, active route/journey and recent canonical Maps entities.
Automations and extensions
Maps may expose automation triggers such as arrive at place, leave place, enter/exit radius, material route-duration change or transit disruption where platform/background capabilities and permissions support them. Persistent/background location requires explicit OS/Home permission and MUST NOT be inferred from ordinary foreground Maps access.
Extensions may add providers, overlays, POI categories, route modes, map layers or specialist geospatial tools through typed capability contracts. Providing a layer/provider does not automatically grant precise location, private landmark access or route history.
Safety, provenance and disclaimer
Maps MUST present map and calculated route data as guidance rather than guaranteed ground truth. A displayed road, path, crossing, entrance, restriction, building, POI or route MUST NOT be represented as guaranteed to exist, be accessible, be legal to use or be safe merely because it appears in provider/community data.
The following compact user-facing disclaimer is required in Maps and MUST be available during route/navigation use: 'Map data is sourced by third party providers and community volunteers. Check important routes.'
A fuller safety/data notice may additionally explain that provider/community data can be incomplete, inaccurate or outdated and that users should follow real-world signs, restrictions and conditions. The compact notice does not replace the product's separately reviewed legal terms.
Community/unverified objects must expose verification/provenance state where relevant and MUST NOT be styled in a way that falsely implies the same confidence as independently established/provider-verified data.
Maps acceptance requirements
* The latest appropriate CoMaps donor baseline is retained/adapted with CUI without losing mature offline/navigation behaviour except where explicitly replaced.
* Open provider interfaces support the agreed default OSM/MapLibre/Pelias/Valhalla stack and allow independent replacement of rendering, search/geocoding, routing, transit, traffic and imagery capabilities.
* Place, Route, SavedPlace, PersonalLandmark, CommunityPOI and SavedRoute/CustomJourney have stable canonical identities usable across 9to1 apps.
* Search mode supports deterministic place discovery/manual route building; AI mode uses Dulche against the same canonical Maps state and typed capabilities.
* Users can drop a pin anywhere, create a private custom landmark, navigate to it, choose structured POI presets and explicitly submit community POIs.
* Community POI duplicate detection, provenance, verification/update lifecycle, reports and routable/searchable behaviour are implemented without silently publishing to OpenStreetMap.
* Saved custom routes support typed travel/stop/wait/activity/manual steps, required/preferred/optional intent, user-defined shortcut/path segments, AI creation/editing and safe sharing.
* Location permissions distinguish approximate/precise/background access and prevent unrelated apps/extensions from inheriting sensitive location data.
* Offline maps remain usable where licences/data permit and do not rely on prohibited bulk use of public community endpoints.
* 9to1://Maps and reusable Maps CUI surfaces integrate with Planner, Events, Boards, Spaces, Write/Present, Forms, Automations, Browse and Dulche.
* The required route/data disclaimer and provenance/freshness states are present; Maps never represents provider/community route data as guaranteed real-world truth.

source_text:
Domain identity and effective source
Every source domain has stable DomainID, ProjectID, type (Main, Branch, Twig or Leaf), parent DomainID where applicable, name, creation/base revision, local revision, effective revision, state, visibility, permission policy and Revision. Renaming or moving display labels MUST NOT change identity.
Effective source is a deterministic projection of the domain's inherited ancestor state plus the domain's own deltas, tombstones, renames and Root/Freeze/Subroot rules. For a Leaf, the conceptual order is Main baseline → Branch delta → Twig delta → Leaf delta.
Each effective file/resource can expose lineage: originating ancestor/domain, inherited revision, local override/delta, rename/delete state, Root authority and any paused/conflicted cascade. View lineage MUST use canonical history rather than infer origin from current path text.
Domain creation, hierarchy guards and reparenting
Hierarchy is enforced by the model/API: Main may create Branches; a Branch may create Twigs; a Twig may create Leaves; a Leaf cannot create children. Main cannot be a child and cannot contain Twigs, Leaves or Subroots.
Creating a child records its exact parent/base effective revision. Later parent changes arrive through cascade processing; the recorded base remains available for history, review and conflict calculation.
Reparenting is not a rename. Moving a Twig to another Branch or a Leaf to another Twig requires an explicit Reparent operation that calculates the new base/effective source, previews conflicts, preserves stable DomainID/history and requires the configured permission. Cross-project reparenting is prohibited; use fork/import/migration workflows instead.
Deletion of a parent with active descendants is blocked unless the operation explicitly archives/prunes/migrates the descendants under the corresponding lifecycle rules.
Materialisation and concurrency model
Stack MUST support opening, browsing, building and acting on multiple domains concurrently without requiring user-facing Git worktree switching. Each active execution/editor receives a domain-scoped materialised view produced from canonical effective source.
Implementations MAY use overlay filesystems, virtual projections, content-addressed materialisation, temporary isolated checkout directories or another robust mechanism, but the materialisation is derived state and MUST NOT become a competing source of truth.
Concurrent writes target stable DomainID/resource identity. Two clients or agents editing the same domain/resource use revision/merge conflict semantics; isolated domains may proceed independently. A failed materialisation or cache rebuild MUST be recoverable from canonical Stack/Git/Files state.
Commit history for Branches, Twigs, Leaves and Subroots
Branches use normal native Git commit history where Git-backed. Twig/Leaf/Subroot changes also have ordered canonical Change/Commit records with stable IDs, parent revision, author/initiator, timestamp, message, affected resources and resulting domain revision.
When GitHub-backed, Twig/Leaf/Subroot commit objects are represented through the protected Stack companion storage/manifest so their history is durable without exposing each nested domain as a normal Git branch. The manifest maps stable Stack change IDs to retained Git object/content identities sufficient for reconstruction.
History for a domain distinguishes inherited ancestor changes from locally authored changes. Rewriting or squashing history is explicit and permission-controlled; it MUST NOT silently invalidate descendants, releases or open Change Requests.

source_text:
Files and GitHub dual-authority/synchronisation
When only Files backing is enabled, Files/Stack canonical metadata and source are authoritative. When only GitHub backing is enabled, native Git state plus protected Stack metadata are authoritative according to the adapter contract.
When both Files and GitHub are enabled, the project config explicitly selects authority mode: Stack/Files primary with GitHub mirror, GitHub primary with Files cache/backup, or managed bidirectional synchronisation. Bidirectional mode uses stable object/revision mapping and MUST surface concurrent divergent edits as sync conflicts; last-writer-wins is not an acceptable default.
Each successful sync records source revision, destination revision and mapping checkpoint. Partial sync leaves a resumable SyncConflict/Failed state and MUST NOT claim both backends are current.
Credentials and private remote metadata use shared credential/security infrastructure rather than being stored in project source.
Git compatibility and advanced Git operations
Git remains an interoperable underlying source-control substrate. Stack supports commit, stage/unstage where relevant, fetch, pull/synchronise, push, revert, cherry-pick, tags, signed commits, history, blame, diff, Git LFS, import/migration and mirrors where compatible.
Raw Git operations that would invalidate Stack-managed lineage, dependency refs or Root/Subroot metadata are blocked or routed through an explicit Advanced/Unmanaged operation that explains consequences and repairs/reconciles Stack metadata before normal work resumes.
Checking out an arbitrary Git branch inside a Stack-managed materialisation MUST NOT silently change the active Stack DomainID. Active domain is controlled by Stack's typed SetActive/OpenDomain operations.
Mixed public/private projection
Visibility is attached to canonical domains/resources and inherited according to explicit policy. Public projection includes only content and history proven public for the selected release/domain projection.
Before public GitHub mirroring, forking or source browsing, Stack validates the projected tree and reachable object/history graph. If private content, credentials, private commit ancestry or private Stack metadata would be reachable, publication is blocked until the exposure is resolved.
Changing a resource from public to private does not retroactively erase already-published Git history. Stack warns when historical exposure exists and offers supported remediation/rewrite workflows without pretending the previous public data was never published.
Team permissions and sensitive operations
Permissions can be set at organisation/project and, where needed, domain level. Core roles/capabilities cover view source, contribute, create child domains, commit, promote/create Change Requests, review/approve, manage Roots/Subroots, manage Freezes, manage releases/packages, administer visibility/remotes and prune/purge.
Child-domain permissions inherit from parent policy unless an explicit narrower override is allowed. A child MUST NOT grant broader access to private ancestor material than the parent/project permits.
Sensitive operations such as permanent purge, private→public exposure, protected-domain override, remote replacement and destructive Root history rewrite require elevated permission and stronger confirmation; project policy MAY require 2FA.

source_text:
Picture
Product role and editing-first boundary
9-1 Picture is the native CUI image creation, editing and composition app for raster, vector and hybrid visual work. Its primary purpose is powerful creation/editing, not passive image viewing. Picture MUST support professional-grade manual editing, simple object-first workflows, non-destructive composition, AI-assisted editing, generative image creation, sketch-to-image conversion and advanced vector tooling while remaining approachable to users who do not want to manage low-level layer structure.
Browsing/viewing/library workflows remain supported but are secondary to Create, Edit and Generate. Core crop/transform/colour/vector/text/drawing/export workflows MUST remain fully usable when AI is disabled, unavailable or disallowed.
Shared-engine reuse and fast feature parity
Picture MUST reuse the mature shared engines already used by Write, Present, Canvas and Boards whenever capability overlaps. It MUST NOT create Picture-private duplicates of shared drawing, text, shape, selection, transform, clipboard, accessibility, undo/history or embedded-object semantics merely for implementation convenience.
Required reuse includes at minimum:
* The Home-owned Shared Productivity Engine for shared text, shapes, media/object identity, selection, transform, clipboard/transfer, accessibility and typed object actions where those semantics apply.
* The Rnote-derived shared drawing/ink engine already used by Canvas and Boards for pens, strokes, pressure/tilt, eraser behaviour, stroke serialisation and drawing selection/manipulation.
* Shared shape/vector primitives, transform handles, snapping/alignment and object manipulation behaviours already exercised by Present/Canvas/Boards where applicable.
* Shared rich-text/typography primitives from Write/Present for editable text objects rather than a second incompatible text engine.
* Shared Files identity/storage, CUI runtime, Home permission/trust, persistent AI bar, revision/action conventions and cross-app artifact references.
Where Picture needs a capability that logically belongs in one of these shared engines, the implementation SHOULD extend that shared engine centrally and enable the new capability for other eligible apps rather than fork it inside Picture. This reuse is a release requirement intended to accelerate feature parity and keep behaviour identical across the ecosystem.
Canonical Picture document model
Picture MUST use a versioned editable PictureDocument rather than treating the current rendered bitmap as the sole source of truth. A document has stable DocumentID, optional backing FileID/source revision, canvas/artboard geometry, colour profile, background, canonical ElementGraph/LayerGraph, linked assets, edit history/revisions, metadata and document revision.
DocumentType supports Raster, Vector and Hybrid. Hybrid documents can contain raster content, editable vector paths/shapes, text, generated objects, masks, drawing/ink, adjustments and linked assets in one document without destructive flattening.
Every independently editable object has stable ElementID plus ElementType, parent/group identity, bounds/transform, visibility, lock state, blend/compositing properties where applicable, mask/effect references, metadata and revision. Renaming/reordering does not change identity.

source_text:
Wave
Product role and native-generation principle
9-1 Wave is the native CUI audio recording, editing, mixing, sequencing and sound-creation app. It combines an approachable multitrack editor with professional waveform/spectral editing, mixing, effects, music sequencing, sound-effect construction, text-to-speech and AI-assisted production.
All generated audio components MUST be native, structured Wave components whenever the requested result can be represented by Wave's own sequencer, synthesis, effect, speech or clip systems. AI MUST NOT normally return an opaque arbitrary waveform as the canonical result for music, sound effects, speech or other structured generative workflows. Rendering to audio is a derived/export/playback result; the editable native component remains canonical.
Example: asking AI to create a song produces editable sequencer/instrument/pattern/arrangement data; asking for a laser sound creates an editable Sound Effect Builder patch; asking for narration creates a native Text-to-Speech object retaining its text/voice/prosody settings.
Shared media/audio engine
Wave MUST share its core audio/media primitives with Motion, Present and other eligible 9to1 surfaces rather than creating incompatible per-app audio engines. The shared media/audio layer owns canonical audio assets, clips, time ranges, transport/playback, waveform/spectrogram analysis, effect descriptors, rendering/export primitives and realtime-safe audio processing where applicable.
Motion uses the same compatible audio clip/effect/timeline primitives for video projects. Present recording/narration uses compatible Wave/shared-media assets. Vision & Voice contributes shared microphone/device discovery, OS audio permissions and applicable capture primitives, while Wave remains the persistent production editor. Dulche Audio/Voice supplies model-backed transcription, analysis and speech capability without becoming a second project model.
GStreamer is an approved maintained media backend and GStreamer Editing Services or an explicitly documented equivalent may be used where appropriate. Backend choice MUST preserve the public Wave project/action contracts.
Canonical project model
WaveProject has stable ProjectID, sample-rate/channel configuration, timeline/timebase, tempo map where used, Tracks[], Markers/Regions[], native generated components, project settings, CreatedAt/ModifiedAt and Revision.
AudioTrack has stable TrackID, name, ordered Clips[], Gain, Pan, Mute, Solo, RecordArm, Effects[], AutomationLanes[], routing/bus state where supported and Revision.
AudioClip has stable ClipID, SourceAssetID or native GeneratedComponentID, source range, TimelineStart, Duration, Gain, fades, stretch/pitch settings, effects/automation references and Revision. Timeline editing MUST be non-destructive by default.
Generated native components receive stable IDs and can be inserted on tracks like other sources while retaining their editable structured source. Rendering a component for playback/export does not replace that structured source.

Motion
Product role and native project principle
9-1 Motion is the native CUI video editing, compositing, animation and motion-graphics application. It combines professional non-linear editing, layered visual composition, animation, titles/graphics, colour, audio production, AI-assisted editing and generative-video workflows while keeping the default editing experience approachable.
The canonical result of work in Motion is a structured MotionProject, not a rendered video. Normal edits such as trimming, crop, speed changes, transforms, masks, effects, colour changes, captions, keyframes, procedural animation and AI-assisted mutations MUST remain inspectable editable project state. Rendering, proxies, previews, caches and exports are derived outputs and MUST NOT silently replace canonical project state.
Shared engines and dependency boundaries
Motion MUST reuse shared 9to1 engines aggressively wherever the underlying capability belongs to more than one product. Shared capability MUST live in the appropriate shared engine/library rather than requiring another app UI process or duplicating private implementations.
Motion reuses the Wave/shared-media engine for audio clips, tracks, waveform/spectrogram analysis, effects, mixing, generated speech/music/SFX and audio rendering; Picture/shared visual primitives for compatible raster/vector composition, masks, paths, still-image effects and object-level image manipulation; Present/shared animation primitives for compatible easing, interpolation and timing concepts; the Shared Productivity Engine for compatible text, vector shape, drawing/ink and transform primitives; Rnote-derived drawing/path primitives for annotation, matte/mask drawing and rotoscoping assistance; Files for canonical asset identity; Dulche/model infrastructure for analysis and generation; the shared Node Graph Framework for advanced graphs; and CUI for the shell/navigation/interaction system.
Dependency direction MUST remain acyclic and engine-oriented. Motion MUST NOT require the Picture or Wave UI processes merely to crop an image or adjust audio. Picture, Wave and Motion consume compatible shared implementations. If Motion needs a capability that Picture, Wave, Present or another surface also materially needs, the implementation SHOULD be placed in the owning shared engine rather than copied.
Canonical project model
MotionProject has stable ProjectID, Sequences[], AssetReferences[], GeneratedComponents[], GlobalSettings, ColourSettings, ProxyCacheSettings, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt and Revision.
Sequence has stable SequenceID, Width, Height, PixelAspectRatio, FrameRate/timebase, Duration, VideoTracks[], compatible AudioTracks[], Markers[], Guides/safe-area state where used, colour/HDR state and Revision.
VisualTrack has stable TrackID, name, ordered Elements[], visibility, lock state, compositing state where applicable and Revision. Audio tracks use compatible Wave/shared-media track primitives rather than a second incompatible audio model.
MotionElement has stable ElementID, ElementType, SourceAssetID or GeneratedComponentID where applicable, TrackID, TimelineStart, Duration, SourceRange, Transform, Crop, Opacity, BlendMode, Masks[], Effects[], ParameterAnimation[], graph references where applicable and Revision.
Masks, EffectInstances, AnimationTracks, Keyframes, Titles/TextObjects, CaptionTracks, CaptionCues, analysis records and Motion node-graph objects MUST have stable identity and revision-aware state where they are addressable/editable. AI, Automations, collaboration and undo/redo address canonical object IDs and properties rather than screen coordinates.

Terminal
Product role and core invariant
9-1 Terminal is the shared first-party terminal runtime and terminal application for 9to1. It provides genuine interactive shell/PTY behaviour plus a distinct natural-language AI execution mode, while preserving the exact security, permission and side-effect boundaries of the underlying action.
Terminal is not an AI chatbot styled as a command prompt. Command Mode remains a normal terminal capable of running existing shell applications unchanged; AI Mode is an additional semantic command/action surface.
Natural-language phrasing MUST NOT lower safety. An operation that is destructive, privileged, externally consequential, credential-sensitive or otherwise high-risk remains equally protected when requested in natural language.
Canonical session model
TerminalSession has stable TerminalSessionID, EnvironmentID, ShellProfileID, mode, process/PTY binding, working directory, title, tab/pane location, command history references, running process/job state, Stack/Dev context where applicable, creation/reconnect metadata and Revision.
Environment identity is explicit. A session always knows whether it targets the local host, WSL, container, SSH host, VM, Dev environment, 9to1-OS host or another registered execution provider.
Display names, tab order and current path are not used as durable session identity.

source_text:
AI execution verification and dangerous-command protection
AI Mode may execute low-risk, clearly resolved actions according to the user's existing trust/permission policy. Potentially dangerous or ambiguous operations require explicit verification before execution.
Verification is mandatory for destructive/bulk-destructive filesystem operations, shutdown/restart, privilege/security changes, process termination with material impact, package/system changes, credential access, permission changes, remote/external mutations and other actions classified as elevated by the owning app/system action.
The verification view states what will run, where it will run, what is expected to change, affected object counts/scopes where determinable and what cannot be predicted. Unknown impact is displayed as unknown rather than omitted.
Ambiguous natural-language requests that could resolve to materially different consequential actions MUST pause for clarification/selection rather than choosing the more destructive interpretation.
AI Mode cannot split one dangerous request into many nominally lower-risk commands to evade Home risk aggregation or approval.
Home permission-broker integration
Protected AI Mode actions use the global Home permission broker. Terminal supplies stable caller/action identity, target app/environment, resolved scopes and risk metadata; it does not implement a weaker private approval system.
Manual Command Mode execution remains ordinary shell execution subject to OS/shell permissions and Terminal-specific guards. Where a shell command crosses a 9to1 protected semantic boundary such as Stack managed infrastructure, the owning product guard still applies.
Always Trust or other Home trust grants never bypass OS elevation, provider authentication, 2FA, Stack protections or product-specific safeguards.

source_text:
Working directory and path semantics
Each session maintains a real working directory appropriate to its environment. Working-directory changes initiated by the shell are tracked through shell integration where available rather than guessed solely from prompt text.
Paths remain native to the environment so existing CLIs work correctly. Files integration adds stable identity/navigation where possible without replacing required filesystem paths.
Drag/drop of a Files item into Command Mode inserts an appropriately escaped native path/reference for the active shell where supported.
Shell integration protocol
Optional first-party shell integration can report command start/end, command text, exit code, working directory, prompt boundaries and other safe semantic state. This allows reliable command/output grouping without fragile ANSI scraping.
Raw PTY operation remains functional when shell integration is unavailable. Terminal MUST NOT require modifying every third-party shell to provide basic terminal behaviour.
Shell integration data is environment-scoped and cannot be trusted as an authorisation signal for privileged operations.
Command and output history
Terminal maintains configurable history for commands and Terminal-native actions, distinguishing user-entered shell commands, AI-executed actions, AI-generated shell commands, $Ask requests, denied/cancelled actions and scheduled actions.
Users can search, filter, copy, rerun eligible commands, pin entries and clear history according to policy. Sensitive commands or outputs can be excluded/redacted.
History records whether an AI suggestion was merely shown, inserted, or actually executed; the UI MUST NOT imply execution from proposal alone.

Failed remote reconnect, scheduled-action creation or app integration leaves explicit recoverable state rather than silently falling back to another environment.
Platform capability behaviour
Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same TerminalSession, mode, AI action and integration model while capability-negotiating local PTY implementation, shells, WSL, OS elevation, SSH/provider and process controls.
Web Terminal requires an authorised remote/server environment provider for real shell execution unless the web platform exposes an approved execution environment. It MUST NOT present browser-side simulation as host terminal access.

SPUI-133 — MODEL REASONING EFFORT DISPLAY
The percentage attached to the model name in the Spaces Chat compact picker (for example “Qwen 3.6 • 100%”) is the currently selected REASONING EFFORT LEVEL for that model/route, NOT quota, remaining usage, context-window fill, confidence, CPU/GPU utilisation or provider health.
The selected effective model's REAL provider/Dulche capability metadata determines the number N of discrete supported effort levels and whether reasoning is enabled/disabled or configurable. Show N distinct user-facing percentage choices, each mapped one-to-one, in increasing order, onto the N actual advertised effort levels:
  N=3: 35%, 70%, 100%.
  N=4: 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%.
  N=5: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%.
For other N, present evenly distributed, legible percentages for each distinct advertised level without inventing unsupported options. The listed 3/4/5 mappings are canonical. Percentages are normalised UI LABELS for discrete provider-specific effort rankings, NOT a literal continuous strength measurement nor a supported percentage of model parameters or context tokens. Displayed options MUST remain bijective to advertised reasoning levels; selecting the first displayed preset MUST invoke the first actual level and not the second. Bind selection to the exact model/provider's stable level identity or ordinal, not to an arbitrary percentage passed through an incompatible floor(p*N/100) formula. When the user changes models, discover the new model's own reasoning/effort options and show only the eligible ones; validate inherited and explicit selections. If a model offers an independent reasoning enabled/disabled switch, honour and display its real on/off state. If no reasoning-effort control exists, do not fabricate a 100% control or suggest that reasoning is configurable. If a provider supplies effort tiers but no on/off switch, do not invent one. Setting changes must affect the actual subsequent Dulche requests and survive the appropriate request/conversation override lifecycle. Fail clearly for unsupported effort settings, never silently assume the backend accepted them.
IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: Existing V2 low-level SetReasoningLevel prose uses min(n−1, floor(p*n/100)) for arbitrary percentage inputs. That function would map the first displayed 35% (for three levels) to the SECOND tier and the first displayed 20% (for five tiers) to the SECOND tier. The canonical user-facing selector must therefore map directly to discrete provider effort LevelIDs/ordinals, not route preset labels through that old formula. Any arbitrary-percent legacy API compatibility must be separately specified/versioned rather than causing incorrect or duplicated preset selection.

SPUI-140 — COUNTING, ENFORCEMENT, FALLBACK, AND LIMIT TRANSPARENCY
User custom budgets MUST provide useful consumption control even when external providers do not expose quota telemetry. 9to1 may count its own authenticated request activity and measured token/tool/message/time metrics via Dulche, while labelling those values as “9to1-observed only” or Estimated when appropriate. It MUST NOT claim those numbers include all outside-provider usage or represent a real provider balance. In accordance with SPUI-136, lack of PROVIDER usage data still hides the compact remote usage arc and uses M, even when local tracked custom-budget usage can be inspected in Home or the indicator's detail surface.
When a custom limit is enforceable for 9to1-originated work, the router MUST check it before starting applicable requests and enforce it with authoritative shared counters for concurrency and retries, not merely grey out the UI. High-risk conflicting provider-side uncertainty must not be passed off as reliable hard cap. Advisory mode may warn without blocking; Hard mode blocks according to declared scope and period. Prior completed/pending actual usage must not be duplicated on retry, fallback or reconnection. When limits cannot be reliably counted/enforced, show “tracking unavailable” or require advisory mode; never promise a hard guarantee.
Provider usage signals can be delayed or partial; show observed-at/freshness and actual reason when a cap is unavailable/exhausted. Usage is attributed to the provider/model that ACTUALLY served the request after any authorised fallback, not simply the originally highlighted selection. Each applicable provider and model budget applies to whichever real backend processes the request, with no unauthorised local-to-cloud fallback.
Provider caps and user caps are independently enforced. Reaching one applicable cap blocks eligible traffic according to the relevant hard policy, even if another allowance still remains. A user-defined limit cannot increase a provider quota, paid entitlement or administrator restriction. Configurable warnings may trigger before thresholds, but their exact preset percentages are not fixed here.

SPUI-143 — DEFAULT LIMIT SELECTION (NO USER PIN)
The Spaces top-header USAGE progress circle presents the single MOST IMMEDIATELY CONSTRAINING applicable limit by the owner's two-stage decision rule, not the highest consumed percentage:
1. DEFAULT PREFERENCE: a SHORTER usage window takes precedence over a longer one (e.g. a five-hour limit is displayed before a weekly limit even if the five-hour cap is 20% used and the weekly cap is 80% used). Compare actual configured duration/windows, not the displayed percentage consumed.
2. SHORTER-WINDOW EXCEPTION: where an applicable longer-window cap has LESS ACTUAL REMAINING ALLOWANCE than the shorter-window cap IN COMPARABLE UNITS, the longer-window cap wins as it will constrain further equivalent use first. Example: weekly has 3,000 TOKENS left, five-hour cap has 5,000 TOKENS left; display weekly despite its longer window. The priority should account for imminent reset when its occurrence makes that cap non-blocking before the expected consumption.
3. Provider-wide and model-specific limits from both provider-reported and owner-defined settings MUST participate if they apply to the current effective model/provider account and have valid measurable data. Honor the source/telemetry visibility rules of SPUI-136: a local model hides usage; a remote model without provider-reported usage hides the compact usage arc and shows M rather than fabricating a fraction, even if a user custom cap can be separately inspected/enforced.
4. Never directly compare raw numeric remaining allowances of INCOMPATIBLE UNITS: tokens are not messages, time is not tool calls. A different-unit cap can outrank another only if a supported, transparent and sufficiently grounded forecast indicates the next effective blocking cap; otherwise use the time-window preference without pretending units are commensurable.
5. Actual blocking rules remain independent: all applicable enforceable caps are checked, regardless of which is displayed in the circle. Display choice must never switch off enforcement of hidden limits.

SPUI-144 — USER-PINNED LIMIT SELECTION
The user MUST be able to PIN exactly one applicable usage limit as the PREFERRED limit displayed in the usage circle. Pin controls belong in the usage breakdown/details popover and/or the corresponding Home model/provider usage settings. Visually distinguish selected pinned limit by a pin symbol and accessible label. Persist a stable canonical LimitID scoped to the relevant user/profile/provider account and model applicability (not the display name or an array index). Display the pinned limit by default regardless of another limit's percent filled, shorter reset window or routine dynamic selection.
PIN OVERRIDE — The pinned choice MUST be temporarily displaced ONLY when another enforceable applicable limit is credibly predicted or known to cause a meaningful, SOONER BLOCK of requests/use than the pinned limit. Example: user pinned five-hour tokens with 5,000 tokens remaining, but a weekly token limit has only 3,000 tokens remaining and is going to be exhausted first; display the weekly limit as an EMERGENT CONSTRAINT. A cap at 80% consumption does NOT override a pinned cap merely because its percentage exceeds the pinned cap's 20%. Account for reset windows and actual effective usage/forecast evidence, not percentages alone. If another limit cannot be confidently assessed, do not pretend there is an emergency.
Do NOT silently delete the stored pin just because an emergency temporarily takes the circle. Surface a clear “Temporarily showing weekly limit; five-hour limit remains pinned” notice, optionally with a warning/urgent symbol. Once the emergency has genuinely cleared (or the competing cap resets/is no longer the next blocker), restore the user's original pinned display automatically if eligible. If user explicitly unpins, the limit is permanently removed/unavailable, their scope changes or its permissions expire, fall back to default selection and explain why the saved preference is not currently active.
A pinned advisory/warning budget MAY be shown as a selected favourite but it MUST NOT supersede an actual imminent HARD cap capable of blocking requests. Multiple simultaneous candidates must be prioritised deterministically; no flickering/ring thrashing on every small telemetry update. Pin does not authorise external usage or change hard-quota enforcement.

Known imminent rejection of the current/next eligible request is sufficient to override a pin regardless of the exact warning horizon.

SPUI-149 — CANONICAL TASK TILE BADGES (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Each task tile displays a contextual PRIMARY task badge with the following owner-selected meanings, symbols and semantic colours (draw using CUI-owned icon/vector assets and current theme/accessibility tokens; emojis below are SYMBOLIC references, not a mandate to use multicolour emoji fonts):
• COMPLETED — tick/check, SHAMROCK green (✅); all agreed work has been produced but full acceptance verification is not yet satisfied.
• VERIFIED — tick/check, GOLD (✓); all agreed work has been produced and every applicable acceptance test passes for the current task/output revision. GOLD is the owner-confirmed distinct primary task-tile badge for VERIFIED; it is not interchangeable with shamrock COMPLETED. If a new requirement, changed output or stale/failed test invalidates verification, immediately withdraw the gold VERIFIED badge and show the truthful current status until reverified.
• UNREAD CHECKPOINT — flag, TURQUOISE (🏴 rendered turquoise). Show ONLY after a checkpoint is reached that the user has not yet viewed. Once the user views the newly reached checkpoint, remove the transient flag and show the task's current applicable progress/status indicator. Re-surface for a newly reached unread checkpoint. BLOCKED OVERRIDES the checkpoint flag.
• WORKING — animated person typing / at-work person (👨‍💻), truthful active substantial execution only. Honour reduced motion and non-animated accessibility fallback; never animate as 'working' when execution is disconnected/paused.
• PERMISSION NEEDED — BLUE shield (🛡️), linked to a real pending authorisation/permission gate; do not grant through appearance alone.
• STALLED — YELLOW warning triangle (⚠️), an unexpected problem the worker is actively trying to resolve without currently needing the user's intervention.
• BLOCKED — RED cross/no-entry (🚫), genuine material inability to proceed without the necessary external/person action. This badge takes precedence over an unread checkpoint flag.
Preserve underlying V2 distinction among raw Task states, execution stages, NEEDS INPUT, CHECKPOINT events, COMPLETED and VERIFIED acceptance status; the badge is a UI projection, not a replacement for the canonical schema. OWNER CONFIRMED 13 OCTOBER 2026: VERIFIED uses the distinct GOLD tick; COMPLETED retains the SHAMROCK-green tick. Continue showing accurate test/evidence status and the existing V2 gold verified checkpoint ticks. A completed-but-unverified Task must not display the VERIFIED gold tick. Other simultaneous-badge precedence beyond BLOCKED > unread CHECKPOINT is not yet owner-decided; maintain visible access to actionable pending approvals/questions regardless of the primary badge chosen.

A user can plan a project in an Assistant's Main conversation and hand it to another conversation with the SAME Assistant to implement, or hand off from one organised conversation to another. The receiving conversation can be new or existing. The handoff carries a visible, inspectable and permission-filtered package of the agreed goal, scope, accepted plan/constraints, relevant messages/source references, task/run identity, checkpoints, outputs, remaining work and applicable acceptance criteria, to the extent legitimately authorised. Do NOT move/copy entire private histories indiscriminately or duplicate external side effects. Original source messages remain in their original conversation, with traceable references. The same canonical Assistant identity and existing TaskID/RunIDs persist if continuing the same work; creating a new task requires an explicit genuinely separate objective. Workers must apply changed instructions at safe boundaries. Proposed affordance “Hand off to Conversation” is a useful UI label but exact menu placement/visual presentation remains OPEN for review.

SPUI-156 — PERSISTENT ASSISTANT TEAMS (OWNER CONFIRMED)
The Assistants Space adds “Teams”: persistent user-created group chats containing multiple selected, existing persistent Assistants. Teams have stable identity, member roster, conversational history and assigned responsibilities. They are NOT merely a one-off Multi-Agent Chat, a Chat Group/Project organisation container, a single new meta-Assistant, a Specialist catalogue, or the Dulche runtime's disposable subagent group. Existing Assistant identities, personal Main conversations and individually authorised resources remain distinct while they participate in Teams. Users may ask a Team to accomplish an outcome, and different members can undertake different roles and Tasks (e.g. a future job split by speciality), coordinated through the existing durable Tasks/Run and Automation/Planner services. Do not force redundant Assistant/Task records for every member or Team message.

SPUI-157 — CONFIGURABLE TEAM COORDINATION (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Team settings MUST provide a user-selectable coordination mode with BOTH alternatives:
• Automatic Dulche Coordination: Dulche allocates relevant work among eligible members, manages dependencies and execution, and does not require a permanent Assistant leader.
• Designated Assistant Leader: user chooses one eligible Team Assistant as leader/coordinator for assignment and delegation while Dulche still enforces routing, permissions, tasks, durable state, resource limits and safety.
Switching mode does NOT discard TeamID, roster, messages, valid TaskID/RunIDs, outputs or accepted checkpoints; in-flight assignment/ownership changes need truthful transitions and no duplicated work. Whether Automatic is the initial default is still PROPOSED (not explicitly owner-confirmed), as are detailed leader absence/fallback and contested delegation resolution policies. Do not silently hard-code them as decisions.

SPUI-158 — RELEVANCE-GATED SELECTIVE PARTICIPATION (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Dulche decides which Team Assistants should participate and respond in any particular request based on relevant role/expertise, actual eligibility and permissions, necessary dependencies and task context. Membership ALONE does not cause every Assistant to reply or consume model resources. Example: requesting a video should ordinarily engage the video-relevant Assistant, NOT a Programmer unless programming becomes useful for that request. Members can be brought in later if the job develops a genuine dependency; don't require irrelevant acknowledgements. A directed @Assistant mention intentionally addresses that member, but still respects permissions/capability constraints and cannot grant unrelated access. This routing rule applies in BOTH coordination modes. An Assistant omitted from the current discussion may continue independently authorised earlier work; absence of its chat reply does not stop existing work. Model-routing decisions, authorised handoffs and resulting worker actions must remain inspectable with correct provenance rather than fabricated participation.

SPUI-160 — “SHOW ASSISTANT-ASSISTANT CHAT” SETTING (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Each Team provides a user-accessible preference named EXACTLY “Show Assistant-Assistant Chat” with exactly THREE available selectable values:
• All — show all eligible Assistant-to-Assistant conversational messages in the Team chat, including routine exchanges where represented as actual conversation messages.
• Relevant — show Assistant-to-Assistant conversation that makes meaningful contributions, deliberates decisions, resolves dependencies or materially affects the Team's current work, while routine coordination may remain in the inspectable canonical Tasks/Action Graph/activity history.
• None — omit Assistant-to-Assistant conversational exchanges from the normal Team chat display; retain user-directed, individually attributed Assistant messages, significant user-facing requests/approvals and independently inspectable task/action evidence.
This controls USER-FACING VISIBILITY of assistant-to-assistant chat only; it does not disable necessary coordination, rewrite/delete original authoritative history, reduce audit/provenance, or conceal safety/permission events. “All” means eligible actual Assistant-to-Assistant CHAT messages, not hidden model internal reasoning, confidential credentials, unrelated private data or unauthorised logs. Apply permissions/redactions in all modes. A user can change the setting without duplicating task work. Reconcile existing message presentation appropriately on switching, without falsifying history; preserve the preference with canonical, account/team-appropriate state. The initial default among All/Relevant/None is NOT YET OWNER-CONFIRMED; the previous suggestion of Relevant was not selected as a default merely by requesting all options be available.

SPUI-163 — ASSISTANTS/TEAMS ACCEPTANCE AND OPEN DECISIONS
Real-runtime acceptance must verify, with actual Assistant and Team objects and canonical IDs:
1. Creating an Assistant provisions ONE durable Main; selecting it after navigating/restarting returns to the SAME Main; secondary threads remain separate; protected Main is not silently destroyed by thread operations.
2. Plan in Main, hand off to a new or existing other thread of SAME Assistant, continue with correct approved plan/TaskID/RunID, preserve origin/history/traceability and avoid duplicated effects.
3. Form a Team from real existing Assistants, keep the Team's identity and conversation across relaunch, distinguish TeamID from AssistantID, Chat Group/Project and TaskID, and preserve individual personal Main histories.
4. Verify both user-selectable coordination modes, authorised leader selection, role-appropriate assignments, accurate dependency handling, switching in flight without lost work or a parallel broker.
5. Request video work from a team with video/programming roles: video-relevant member participates, programmer stays quiet unless genuinely useful; member dynamically joins on a real dependency; direct mention remains scoped/secure.
6. Verify each relevant member's user-facing reply appears as an individually attributed message, no duplicate combined Team impersonation, no fabricated replies from inactive members.
7. Verify “Show Assistant-Assistant Chat” exposes All / Relevant / None exactly, changing the Team chat visibility correctly while preserving auditability, provenance, approvals, security and context separation. Ensure None does not suppress individually attributed messages to the USER or safety-critical approvals.
8. Verify assistant and Team memory isolation, authorisation, task/worker resource limits, history retention, accessible CUI controls, focus/touch, responsive layout and Professional/Glow inheritance; mark untested cases NOT RUN, not VERIFIED.
OPEN BEFORE FINAL UI/BEHAVIOUR LOCK: exact default Show Assistant-Assistant Chat mode; initial Team coordination default; Main label rename policy and preservation UX; handoff picker/confirmation and branching details; permanent-Team conversation organisation beyond primary group chat; member roster editing/conflict and leader absence; which coordination exchanges count as “Relevant” in edge cases; exact pixel layout/controls. SPUI-164 — RESEARCH CHAT-TO-WORKSPACE TRANSITION (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Opening a new Research conversation initially presents the normal Spaces Chat-like conversation view and floating composer. The user enters a research request and sends it. The SAME Research conversation then transitions into its richer research workspace (do not create a disconnected Chat or Task) with the Plan tab automatically selected, showing a GENERATED REVIEWABLE RESEARCH PLAN. Plan generation must not be misrepresented as final research output. The user can inspect and request/edit plan changes before approving execution. The workspace's primary sections are Conversation, Sources, Plan, Findings and Report; conversation may be presented as a clickable conversation tile, and selecting that tile opens the full normal conversation view, retaining its ConversationID/history/drafts. Switching back to the research workspace preserves active research work and sections. Outputs/Artefacts may also be exposed where relevant and permitted. The source/plan/findings/report content is live canonical information, with honest loading/empty/in-progress/stale/error states rather than generated placeholders presented as truth. Exact arrangement of tab and conversation tile remains subject to CUI visual refinement; user's supplied Research workspace example illustrates the intended high-level structure.
A FLOATING CHAT BAR stays available at the BOTTOM of the research workspace and normal conversation view for additional information, requests, steering, follow-up turns and appropriate attachments, using shared Spaces composer behaviour and the universal send-action contract below. The workspace does not become read-only or require leaving the current research to add context.

SPUI-166 — CHOOSE DELIVERABLES AND START (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Before executing the reviewed plan, the user chooses a desired output:
• REPORT — research findings, evidence, citations/provenance, method and limitations as an inspectable report;
• REPORT & ARTEFACTS — the report PLUS applicable authentic delivered artefacts such as code, experiments/tests, datasets, prototypes, models, notes, Write/Data/Present/Dev objects or other app-native results needed for the agreed research objective.
Either output choice is available in any applicable research type, subject to genuine capabilities and permissions; especially for Custom, Research may solve a substantive technical problem through research, implementation and testing rather than merely writing prose. Use actual owning-app typed APIs and canonical artefact identities; do not simulate artefacts or declare success from speculative tests. Research begins after the user selects/reviews the plan, execution profile and outputs and authorises the run. A research turn is a durable Task/Run when substantive, preserving plan, steps, source sets, outputs, execution stage, permissions, checkpoints, acceptance and model/worker provenance. Deliver the work and expose results in the same Research workspace, including citations and access to genuine exported/openable artefacts.

SPUI-167 — ACTIVE EXECUTION TIME, NOT WALL-CLOCK TIME (OWNER CONFIRMED)
All four research-time profiles, particularly CUSTOM's 28-day maximum per turn, are measured by CUMULATIVE ACTIVE EXECUTION time for the authorised turn, NOT calendar time or wall-clock duration since clicking Start. Count genuine AI reasoning/generation, retrieval/source evaluation, authorised tools and actively executing experiments/tests. Exclude idle waiting for user permission/questions, paused execution, disconnected/unavailable execution hosts, unavailable compute without an actual running job, and similar nonworking idle periods. A genuinely running experiment can count while progressing even if no chat tokens are generated.
Parallel workers' overlapping execution intervals count as the union of active time, NOT the sum of every worker's elapsed durations (three workers working simultaneously for 10 minutes do not consume 30 active minutes). Independently record visible active time versus wall-clock elapsed/wait time and preserve counters across restart, fallback, pause/resume and reconciliation without double-counting. Account separately for tokens, compute/provider usage, spend, rate caps and other resource constraints; an active-time budget does not override them. The UI MUST NOT equate time used with percent of objective completed. At budget exhaustion, halt at a suitable safe boundary, preserve authentic partial work/evidence and remaining plan, report actual result/verification status, and offer permitted follow-up/extension without claiming the work finished or VERIFIED.

SPUI-168 — RESEARCH EXECUTION AND RESEARCH FOLLOW-UP (OWNER CONFIRMED)
While the run is authorised and active, Research shows its plan, real source set, interim qualified findings, outputs, actual checkpoint/verification state, working/waiting/blocked status and true time accounting, in contextual workspace sections. There is always a route back to the full conversation. An active Research conversation accepts further messages through its floating chat composer.
DEFAULT WHEN AN ACTIVE RESEARCH RUN EXISTS: sending another normal message STEERS THE CURRENT RESEARCH, not automatically initiating a second Research turn or discarding valid work. A request such as “also consider papers from 2024 onward” is retained and applied by the same Task/Run at the next safe boundary, with affected plan/scope/checkpoints/tests revised explicitly and received-versus-applied state visible. The user can also choose to QUEUE a follow-up turn for after present execution. Starting a truly separate new research task/conversation remains a distinct explicit action. Once the current research completes, a further research instruction can start a new research turn with its own selected budget and deliverables while preserving prior evidence/history. Universal composer settings/shortcuts under SPUI-169/170 control the selected Steer/Queue send action per Space.

SPUI-169 — UNIVERSAL SPACES STEER / QUEUE WITH PER-SPACE DEFAULT (OWNER CONFIRMED)
ALL applicable conversation-capable Spaces, built-in and user-created, inherit a shared two-mode message submission behaviour for an ongoing response, active agentic run or other applicable execution:
• STEER — send a new instruction to the CURRENT active response/Task/Run to influence work in progress at the next safe supported boundary, preserving accepted work/permissions/checkpoints and reporting whether it was received or actually applied;
• QUEUE — retain the new message/instruction as a genuine QUEUED follow-up for the conversation/eligible run, to be consumed after the current activity reaches its appropriate completion/safe boundary, without interrupting the active response or falsely claiming it has already been processed.
A USER-CONFIGURABLE PREFERRED SEND ACTION MUST exist INDEPENDENTLY FOR EACH SPACE. The preferred value (Steer or Queue) determines that Space's normal send/Enter behaviour during an eligible ongoing response/run, rather than being one global default for every Space. This preference persists across navigation, app restarts and supported user/account synchronisation under existing Home/Spaces preference ownership and Space Overrides > User Preferences > Default precedence; do not alter unrelated preferences or let one Space override another. Expose the selected action visibly and let users switch between Steer/Queue within the composer when applicable. The Research Space preferred/default behaviour at the current owner confirmation is STEER during active research. For other Spaces, the precise initial fallback choice when no preference exists remains OPEN for owner review; do not silently assert one global default. If no compatible ongoing run exists, retain ordinary new-message submission semantics, rather than inventing an active task or claiming steering applied. A user can still explicitly start a separate task under existing Task contracts; that is not a third value of the Steer/Queue preference.
The Steer and Queue contract never grants new permissions, bypasses input/approval gates, expands an Assistant/Team or model's context scope, silently duplicates runs or triggers prohibited tool effects. Preserve the ability to inspect queued messages and change/cancel a still-pending item where supported, with accurate lifecycle/provenance.

SPUI-170 — ALT+ENTER INVERTS THE CURRENT SPACE'S SEND ACTION (OWNER CONFIRMED)
While Steer/Queue is applicable, pressing ALT+ENTER submits the current composer message using the OPPOSITE action from the Space's stored preferred default for that submission only: Steer default -> Alt+Enter QUEUES; Queue default -> Alt+Enter STEERS. It must NOT change or reset the stored preference. Normal Enter/send uses the preferred action. A user-selected one-off action in the composer should remain plainly distinguishable from changing the durable default. Keep existing Shift+Enter/multiline text-entry, focus, IME composition and accessibility rules intact. Offer pointer/touch/keyboard-discoverable equivalent controls and shortcuts/help text for non-Alt+Enter clients. If a platform/IME reserves or intercepts the chord, the UI must expose a working equivalent and report compatibility truthfully rather than pretending the shortcut executed. When no eligible run exists, do not falsely indicate that Steer or Queue was executed or create phantom tasks; handle that inactive-context case as normal conversation submission under the existing Spaces contract.

SPUI-173 — CONVENTIONAL SHOPPING FILTERS PLUS NATURAL-LANGUAGE CONTROL (OWNER CONFIRMED)
The Shopping workspace MUST expose working search/filter/sort controls appropriate to actual products, including PRICE RANGE, FILTERABLE FEATURES/SPECIFICATIONS, DELIVERY TIME, SHIPPING COST, BRAND and other category-relevant attributes (e.g. colour, platform, edition, condition, seller/availability where applicable). SPUI-174 — REQUIRED VERSUS PREFERRED CONSTRAINTS (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Every applicable user search criterion/filter can be explicitly marked REQUIRED or PREFERRED, with effective semantics visible and user-editable. The user can declare them in a prompt or select/change them directly in the filter interface; the assistant can interpret natural language, but must not silently harden a preference into a mandatory criterion, or overlook an explicit hard constraint. Examples: “black hairdryer under £100, preferably next-day delivery” means black + price cap REQUIRED and next-day delivery PREFERRED unless the user revises them. A product satisfying all VERIFIED/KNOWN REQUIRED conditions may be a DIRECT RESULT even if it lacks a preferred property; preferred matches influence ranking/explanations rather than mandatory eligibility. If available evidence does not establish a mandatory feature, never claim the product definitively meets it. Changing Required/Preferred must immediately and honestly recompute categorisation, rankings, match explanations and where relevant product/offer counts from actual data.

source_text:
SPUI-175 — THREE PRIMARY RESULT CATEGORIES (OWNER CONFIRMED)
At the top level of the product-results workspace the three named sections/tabs are EXACTLY: “Direct Results” | “Similar Results” | “Other”.
DIRECT RESULTS: products whose documented, currently supported attributes meet all current REQUIRED constraints, whether or not every PREFERRED feature is present. The product must be real and its claimed specifications, delivery and offer data grounded; do not pad this tab with unverified supposedly exact matches.
SIMILAR RESULTS: relevant alternatives meeting some, but not all, required criteria, with clear per-product disclosure of the specific missing/mismatched REQUIRED properties, unknown fields, and useful matching features. Example: a blue hairdryer with a disinfection feature when the user requested black; it belongs here if black is Required. If black is only Preferred, the same blue hairdryer may qualify as Direct, with its preference shortfall explained.
OTHER: carefully relevant recommendations based on the present shopping intent PLUS legitimate, permission-eligible history/preferences/context. Example: after previous discussion of a broken fridge, smart-fridge results may be contextually relevant when currently shopping for smart toasters; unrelated gloves/shoes must NOT surface merely because they were also mentioned historically. Other must not masquerade as fulfilment of required search constraints, exploit sensitive context, or expose unauthorised memories. Keep the explanation for why a related suggestion appeared inspectable and provide appropriate normal memory/personalisation controls under existing Home/Dulche policy. “Other” is a relevance-gated discovery surface, not indiscriminate advertising, and must still meet source-truthfulness rules.
All three tabs use actual product records and user/session requirements; switching tabs must not reset filters or lose the conversation. Where no results qualify, show an honest empty state and offer appropriate refinements rather than fabricate matches.

SPUI-176 — PHYSICAL, DIGITAL, APPS, GAMES AND NONTRADITIONAL SHOPPING (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Shopping MUST support BOTH physical and digital goods when relevant to the user's intent. Product discovery, comparisons, saved items, price/rating/offer views, filters and results categories must work for DIGITAL PRODUCTS, SOFTWARE/APPLICATIONS and GAMES as first-class shopping categories; do not restrict results to physical items, hardware or traditional shopping. Category-aware filters should surface grounded relevant metadata as applicable, such as supported operating system/device/platform, version or edition, licence/subscription/one-time purchase model, access/delivery/activation method, digital ownership or entitlement scope, regional restrictions, interoperability/compatibility, seller/storefront, update/support information and bundled extras or downloadable content where genuinely supported. These are representative applicable fields, not a requirement that all products have all metadata or that all merchants/marketplaces be supported.
Shipping, shipping cost and physical delivery filters must adapt sensibly to DIGITAL listings; show Not Applicable or digital fulfilment/activation timing as appropriate, NEVER fictional shipping charges or physical delivery promises. The same required-versus-preferred matching logic applies across physical and digital listings. For apps/games, distinguish a purchasable external digital listing from a user's installed/owned 9to1 or third-party app, and identify actual edition/platform/store restrictions; do not fabricate cross-platform compatibility, keys, available subscriptions or entitlements. Display real authorised product/offer data and obey applicable age, regional, merchant, licensing, permissions, account security and purchasing requirements. Shopping discovery never silently purchases, downloads, installs, subscribes or authorises access; consequential actions require the canonical verified review and approval flow.

SPUI-178 — PRODUCTS VERSUS MERCHANT OFFERS; CONTEXTUAL COMPARISON AND INTEGRATION
Preserve a distinction between the identity/specification of an underlying product and particular merchant/storefront offers (price, currency, stock/availability, delivery terms, region, edition, condition, seller/source). The UI must avoid conflating two distinct editions, digital licences or physical variants merely because titles look similar. User-facing grouping is STILL OPEN: whether to show one card per product with offers inside, one card per merchant offer, or a selectable switch. SPUI-196 — DULCHE BUILT-IN SAFETY BLOCK: CONTEXTUAL LOW-OVERHEAD CHECKS
Build an efficient, integrated safety layer for Dulche that does not normally stall harmless generation. A lightweight CPU-friendly streaming detector MAY flag risk signals/patterns, but simple blacklisted WORDS, WORD PAIRS or short topic lists are NOT sole evidence of policy violation. Words with common benign legal, educational, historical, fictional or technical uses must receive CONTEXTUAL classification rather than automatic refusal. Use layered policy: concise consistent baseline guidance to models (not a pretend exhaustive few-hundred-token “security wall”); streamed output checks; contextual risk assessment; independent pre-execution tool-call/app/permission/scope checks; and where uncertainty or high risk warrants, isolated peer-model or authorised human review. Assessment should consider user intent, whether a request is actually prohibited, severity, legitimate educational/helpful exceptions, and the true capabilities of the chosen model/tool. A reviewer may run asynchronously AFTER low-risk material where safe; genuinely high-risk material/tool actions can be HELD before output or execution. Display “Checking Compliance” only when an actual review/pause occurs, with truthful state rather than cosmetic delay. Response latency should be optimised and measured rather than promising zero overhead or relying exclusively on text scanning. SPUI-200 — PEER REVIEW MAX REVIEW TIME: PRECISE ACTIVE-TIME DENOMINATOR (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Resolve SPUI-188 and the former SPUI-199 open question definitively. “Max Review Time: 25% of Task” means: for every X minutes of ACTUAL PRODUCTIVE TASK EXECUTION WORK, the allowed cumulative time spent by peer-review models is at most 25% × X (or the user-selected configured percentage). At 4 hours productive work, up to 1 hour aggregate review work is allowed. Formal budget equation: R <= (p/100) × W, where W is real productive active task-work duration EXCLUDING reviewer execution, waiting, pausing, approvals, idle time or merely keeping a host connected; R is AGGREGATE REAL ACTIVE PEER-REVIEW EXECUTION DURATION across all reviewer instances, not an independent allowance per reviewer. Review after each checkpoint or adaptive intervals draws from the SAME budget, including deliberation with workers, reinspection and intervention-related review activity; reviewers must not hide their time in the worker counter or create additional independent caps. Active overlapping productive worker intervals use an honest canonical task clock rather than summing simultaneous worker durations to artificially inflate W; track actual review-resource cost separately when parallel reviewers operate.
Show used/allowed peer-review time and remaining headroom clearly, update using actual measured Task/Run events, and allow the user to change the percentage subject to policy/resource caps and explicit authorisation. This percentage is an overhead LIMIT, NOT a quota peer review must consume and NOT a guarantee of review completeness. If the remaining budget is exhausted, do not silently keep spending reviewer time, pretend a review was performed or mark acceptance VERIFIED. Necessary policy/permission/independent-review gates still apply: suspend only the risky gated action, continue safe independent work where valid, or seek explicit authorised adjustment/review capacity. Never use budget exhaustion to bypass a required human approval, acceptance test or safety review. Validate worker clock, reviewers with different model backends, parallel reviews, pause/restart/reconnection and partial review recovery without duplicate accounting. The default percentage can be user-configured; the owner-confirmed example is 25%.

SPUI-201 — SINGLE CANONICAL SPACE, THREE FREELY SWITCHABLE BUILDER TABS (OWNER CONFIRMED)
The full Custom Space Creator/Builder MUST expose three peer-level tabs labeled EXACTLY “Basic” | “Advanced” | “Expert”. They are ALTERNATIVE EDITOR VIEWS of ONE canonical UserCreated Space with the SAME SpaceID, settings, graph, permissions, attached resource identities and revision history; they are NOT separate Space types, activation tiers or one-way upgrades. Users can freely switch at any time, including AFTER creating Expert-only graph behaviours. Switching MUST NOT drop, overwrite, flatten, disable or regenerate logic configured in another tier. Basic/Advanced modify only the settings that those views expose, preserving Expert-only nodes and connections; a conflict between a simplified control and a more complex Expert graph must be previewed and explicitly resolved instead of silently choosing a winner or deleting nodes. In simplified editors, surface a subtle clear status such as “Expert configurations active” at the bottom when behaviour exists beyond what the current view represents. The indicator links to relevant Expert sections and must not be treated as a reason to lock or hide Basic/Advanced. All three views persist as projections of the same Draft/Active revisioned configuration and use typed APIs, not separate saved configs.

SPUI-205 — EXPERT USES THE EXISTING 9TO1 AUTOMATIONS NODE SYSTEM (EXPLICIT OWNER CONFIRMATION)
ALL Expert visual logic pages MUST reuse the EXISTING 9to1 HOME-OWNED NODE GRAPH FRAMEWORK, as in AUTOMATIONS, not a new separate or proprietary graph engine. Shared contracts include stable GraphID/NodeID/PortID, typed ports/connections, same registered node schemas, pan/zoom, selection, grouping, search, drag/connect, undo/redo, copy/paste, validator, Draft/Active revision, runtime visualisation, persistence, keyboard/touch accessibility, and shared theme materials. The 13 October supplied 9to1 node-system mockup shows six recognisable node-category examples: TRIGGER (red), CONDITION (orange), EVENT (green), LOGIC (blue), APP (purple), FILES (brown). These six names and visually distinct category treatments are to be recognisable in the Builder's node palette. Screenshot colours/shapes are a design reference; actual accessible node styling and semantic category tokens are owned by the active CUI theme rather than fixed colour hex codes or forced exact screenshot pixel geometry; do not rely on colour alone. Actual executable nodes must be registered against valid typed node APIs. The presence of a mockup “Trigger/Condition/Event/Logic/App/Files” card is NOT evidence that a particular action/node already exists; unsupported nodes show truthful availability and authoring validation.
The Automations framework is the SHARED graph editor/validator/presentation engine, while Spaces owns Space-specific semantics and Dulche/Apps/Files execute authorised typed actions. A Space graph cannot invent a new permission authority, model backend, memory broker or scheduler. Preserve published protected built-in-Space hooks; user-created Spaces receive the full permitted capability profile subject to safeguards.

SPUI-208 — USER MESSAGE LOGIC: NONDESTRUCTIVE INPUT PIPELINE (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Expose full node editor for message-level logic such as TRUNCATE USER MESSAGE, EXTRACT ALL NUMBERS, SEARCH FOR WORDS/PHRASES, parse structured inputs, produce booleans/branches, transform/normalise, filter, match conditions, route and construct context within authorised scope. Source USER MESSAGE must remain immutable in original canonical MessageID/history. Nodes work on explicit derived representations/versioned outputs with inspectable transformation provenance, not retroactively rewriting the user's stored message, losing quoted sources or modifying past external actions. Truncation must signal what was omitted; numeric extraction must specify locale/format uncertainty; word matching must have documented matching semantics; filters cannot leak unauthorized messages to app/tool/MCP endpoints. Support node-level preview, sample input validation, tracing and failure handling; the complete processing chain is constrained by protected security/consent requirements, even in Expert mode.

+ New Space and existing Edit Spaces lead into the same Builder capability, with normal existing stable SpaceID, parent/nesting, ownership, sharing and sidebar customisation. Expose REAL Preview, Validate and Activate/Create actions as separate states. A draft can be previewed with a clearly isolated test conversation and safe mockable inputs; label mocks explicitly and require consent for any genuinely live app/tool/model call or consequential external effect. Versioned revision history and rollback must preserve relevant conversations, TaskIDs, run history, sources and external side effects; never suggest reverting a graph undoes effects already performed. “Schedule” or automatically triggered behaviour uses canonical Automations, not a private Space timer. SPUI-211 — BUILDER REAL-RUNTIME ACCEPTANCE; OPEN VISUAL DETAILS
Independent acceptance MUST exercise:
1. User creates/opens/edits one persistent user Space; Basic, Advanced and Expert switch repeatedly with SAME SpaceID and without losing ANY graph nodes, capability bindings, draft/active changes or Expert-only behaviour. Verify visible “Expert configurations active” hint within Basic/Advanced when appropriate.
2. Basic saves name/description/icon/instructions, enabled/disabled Skills/Plugins/Apps/Models/Memory, and Files/Skills/Plugin additions with truthful permission states.
